**«Osvaldo de Franceschi d'anni 27 ventisette, Servitore» — twice, in his own hand, at Muina.**

**Act N. 12, 10 September 1814** and **act N. 13, Saturday 26 November 1814**, both drawn at the *Agenzia Comunale di Mione* for deaths in the frazione of **Muina**. The same two witnesses both times: **Osvaldo de Franceschi, 27, servant**, and **Fabris Giovanni, 41, also a servant**, *«non parenti, ma vicini del Defunto»*. Both acts are signed **«Osvaldo de Franceschi»** in a large upright hand that is plainly not the registrar's.

**The age is the prize.** Twenty-seven in late 1814 means born **1786–87** — which is what the October 1806 act says (about nineteen) and what both 1809 acts say (twenty-two). The 1810 act, alone, would put him at 1784. **Four against one**, and the window for finding his baptism in the Pieve di Gorto books narrows to two years.

**The identification is not settled.** In 1809 he is a *carpenter* «di Mione»; in 1814 a *servant* and a **neighbour at Muina**. Mione and Muina are 784 m apart, and the signatures look to me like one hand — but that is an opinion, not a finding, and the household tables have not been merged on it.

*The volume has no Tavola Alfabetica — 1813 and 1815 do. The negative for the rest of 1814 is a page-level sweep and is weaker than the 1813 one.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Morti» 1812 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the 1812 death register — swept leaf by leaf, the volume having no alphabetical table
rows.got:
**One act, and it carries two men of the surname signing their own names.**

**Monday 18 August 1812, eight in the morning.** Matteo Lupieri views the body of **Ottaviani Valentino**, twenty-five, a tailor of Mione, dead the previous day. The two men who come to identify him are:

> *«Erman de' Franceschi **Gio: Pietro** d'anni cinquantanove, **Possidente**, e de' Franceschi **Paolo** d'anni **quarantadue**»*

**Paolo is the husband whose house Anna dies in three years later.** Forty-two in 1812 → born about **1770**; Anna was forty-four in November 1815 → born about **1771**.

**Gio: Pietro Erman de Franceschi is now a «Possidente»** — a landowner — where in 1808 and 1809 he was an *agricoltore*. Between those acts sits his marriage to Orsola de Franceschi. Born 28 April 1752, he should be sixty here, not fifty-nine; the year's slack is recorded, not smoothed.

**And he signs «Erman de' Franceschi Gio: Pietro».** Byname first, in his own hand, as he did in 1809. *Erman* at Mione is a **branch-name inside the surname**, not the separate family this archive has been treating it as — which re-reads the 1679 headmen's list and makes every «Erman» entry in the Mione indexes a candidate.

Paolo signs too, smaller and less practised: **«paolo de Franceschi»**, lower-case p.
ev: Two men sign the same page

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni» 1813 and 1814, alphabetical tables (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi marriage in 1813 or 1814, read off each volume's own «Tavola Alfabetica»
rows.got:
**Nine marriages in two years, and none of them ours.**

The method that broke open the death registers works on the marriage registers too: **from 1813 each volume ends with a ruled table** giving surname and forename of both parties, the frazione, the date, the act number and the folio. Two pages answered what would otherwise have been twenty.

**1813 — five marriages** (ark an_ua667522, image 11): Del Fabro Gio: Giacomo × Maria de' Prato, Agrons, 26 Feb · **Erman** Mar.o × Maria Fran.ca de' Prato, Agrons, 29 Aug · Fabris Ant.o × Gortan Maddalena, Ovasta, 28 Sept · Gortan Ant.o × Rupil Maddalena, Luincis, 7 Oct · Corpo Micoli Daniele × Micoli Toscano Maria, Muina, 22 Sept.

**1814 — four marriages** (ark an_ua667523, image 9): one at Chialina 6 June · one at Muina 16 Aug · one at Entrampo 29 Sept · one × Lupieri Giovanna at Luint 21 Oct.

**One row to come back to.** The 1813 *Erman* marriage is at **Agrons**, not Mione — but this archive established today that at Mione **«Erman de' Franceschi» is one signed name**, so Erman rows can no longer be passed over as a neighbouring family without looking.

*Matrimoni 1812 (11 images) and 1815 (5 images) have no tables and are still to be swept.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Pubblicazioni di matrimonio» 1815 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Opened by mistake while hunting for the birth registers — and it is the richest Mione series found yet
rows.got:
**A son for Paolo, a maiden name for Anna, and nine volumes nobody had opened.**

**Sunday 4 June 1815, ten in the morning.** Matteo Lupieri reads the promise aloud and nails it to the town-hall door:

> *«…la promessa di Matrimonio tra **de' Franceschi Felice Santo**, di professione **Sartore**, nativo e domiciliato nella Frazione di **Mione**, … **figlio di de' Franceschi Paolo e di Anna nata Brunis** giugali, e di **de' Canova Lucia Santa**, figlia del fu Osvaldo Antonio e Lucia nata Pellia…, di condizione Possidente, nata e domiciliata nel Villaggio di **Liariis, agenzia d'Ovaro**.»*

**Felice Santo is new** — Paolo's son, and the **fourth tailor** of the surname at Mione.

**«Anna nata Brunis» settles a question this archive published as open the day before.** She married into the surname; the 1815 death act's *«Anna de Franceschi»* is her husband's name, not hers. Logged as a correction.

**And the series matters more than the act.** A Napoleonic banns notice names **both parties, their trades, their villages and all four parents**, with *«del fu»* marking the dead. Mione has one volume a year, **1806–1815, arks an_ua667544–667552**, fifty-odd images, entirely unread.

**The marriage itself is not in Mione's 1815 register.** The bride is of Liariis; under the code the act belongs to the bride's comune, so it should be in **Ovaro's** 1815 marriages — with allegati carrying a baptismal extract out of the Pieve di Gorto.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Pubblicazioni di matrimonio» 1812, act N. 4 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the 1812 banns — the second volume of the series opened
rows.got:
**The deepest De Franceschi couple this project holds from Carnia outside the 1679 list.**

**Sunday 9 August 1812** (published again **16 August**), at the outer door of the town hall of Mione: the promise of marriage of **Zanelli Giambattista**, *«d'anni trentadue compiti»* — thirty-two exactly, born about **1780** — a **tailor** of **Ovasta**, to **Roder Lucia**, twenty-one, of the same village.

The groom is *«figlio delli viventi **Zanelli Francesco** delli fu Pietro e Isola nata Valle, e di **Ottavia nata de' Franceschi**, figlia **delli fu Batta de' Franceschi, e Maria nata Brenis**, giugali»*.

**Three generations in one sentence.** Ottavia, born a de' Franceschi, bearing a son about 1780 — so born herself about **1750–60**. And her parents **Batta de' Franceschi × Maria née Brenis**, dead by 1812, therefore **born in the 1720s or 1730s**.

**They appear nowhere else.** Not in the Mione births, marriages, or the deaths 1806–1815, all now read. A clerk had to say whose daughter the groom's mother was, and that is the only reason this archive has them.

**Ottavia is also a married-out daughter recovered from the wrong end** — not from her own marriage act but from her son's banns. That is a method: where a daughter's marriage is missing, her children's banns will name her, with her maiden surname and her father's.

**And «Brenis» corroborates yesterday's correction.** Paolo's wife was read as *«Anna nata Brunis»*; here is the same surname a generation earlier. The family is already in these books as **Brenci** (the single act of the 1806 death register) and **Brencis** (Cattarina, wife of Osvaldo the carpenter; Agostino, witness in 1808).

*The marriage act itself should be in Mione's own Matrimoni 1812 — ark an_ua667521, eleven images, not yet read — because Ovasta is a frazione of this comune.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Pubblicazioni di matrimonio» 1811 and 1814 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Any De Franceschi in the 1811 and 1814 banns — both volumes swept leaf by leaf
rows.got:
**Twenty pages, no De Franceschi in any role — not as a party, not as a parent.**

**1811** (ark an_ua667548, thirteen images) and **1814** (ark an_ua667551, seven images) were swept page by page at a magnification that shows a name of that length clearly. The surnames that do appear are **Rupil, Rugo, Gortani, Steffani, Bulfon, Fiorenzi, Zanelli, Colledan, Nino, Della Pietra, Vernier, Marcuzzi, Barazzutti, Sivilotti, Roder** and **Zorzi**.

Recorded because a negative in this series is worth more than a negative elsewhere: **a banns notice names four parents**, so a year with no De Franceschi in the banns is a year in which no child of this family married *and* no De Franceschi daughter's child married either.

*Still to sweep: the banns for 1806, 1808, 1809, 1810 and 1813 — fifty-five images.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Pubblicazioni di matrimonio» 1808 and 1809 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The banns behind the two marriages this archive already holds — and what they add
rows.got:
**Two notices, both of them ours, and one of them settles an argument from yesterday.**

**1808, act N. 1 — Sunday 17 January, ten in the morning** (ark an_ua667545, image 3): *«la promessa di matrimonio di **Osvaldo de Franceschi, d'anni venti**, domiciliato nel villaggio di **Muina**, di professione agricoltore, **figlio di Antonio de Franceschi** … **e di Maria nata Corva**, economa di casa, domiciliati in Muina, con **Appolonia Galante** dell'età d'anni **venticinque e mezzo** … figlia di **Antonio Galante e di Speranza Micoli**»* — and the *Avviso* adds *«il matrimonio sarà celebrato li vent'otto Gennajo corrente nel Villaggio di Muina»*.

**«Galante» twice more, in a clear looped G.** The count against *Salante* goes from four hands to **six**.

**And the age settles which Osvaldo stood at Muina in 1814.** Born 14 March 1788, he is nineteen years ten months here and called **twenty**; twenty-six and a half in September 1814 and called **twenty-seven**. Same rounding, six years apart. Logged as a correction, together with the withdrawal of yesterday's signature comparison.

**1809, act N. 1 — Sunday 29 January, nine in the morning**, published *«sulla piazza comunale»* (ark an_ua667546, image 3): *«**Erman de' Franceschi Gio: Pietro**, d'anni cinquantasei, agricoltore … figlio delli defunti **Erman Pietro e Maddalena nata de' Franceschi** jugali, **furono villici di professione, già domiciliati nello stesso villaggio**, con **Orsola de' Franceschi** dell'età d'anni quaranta, villica … figlia delli estinti **Pietro de Franceschi e Maddalena nata Fedeli** jugali»*.

Every name matches the marriage act of **13 February 1809** — so the banns ran **fifteen days** ahead of the wedding. What is new is small and human: the groom's dead parents are described as **villici**, peasants, who had lived in that same village.

*1813 swept: five marriages, no De Franceschi, matching the alphabetical table.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Pubblicazioni di matrimonio» 1806, 1810 and 1813 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The last three unswept banns volumes — completing the series 1806–1815
rows.got:
**Thirty-one more images, no De Franceschi — and with that the series is finished.**

**1806** (an_ua667544, 3 images) opens thin: a title leaf, a blank, and one notice. **1810** (an_ua667547, 13 images): Steffani, Lungo, Nassivera, Micoli, Fabris, Screm, Gortani, Trifoni, Colledan. **1813** (an_ua667550, 15 images): nothing, and the marriage volume's own alphabetical table agrees — five marriages that year, none of them ours.

**The whole run now stands read: nine volumes, ninety-one images, 1806 to 1815, four De Franceschi notices.** 1808 (Osvaldo × Appolonia Galante), 1809 (Erman de' Franceschi × Orsola), 1812 (Ottavia and her parents), 1815 (Felice Santo and his).

*The five negative volumes were swept page by page rather than transcribed. The 1813 one is confirmed independently by the alphabetical table; the other four rest on the sweep alone, and a name buried mid-sentence as a grandparent could have escaped it.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni» 1812 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The Zanelli × Roder marriage act, which should name Batta de' Franceschi and Maria Brenis a second time
rows.got:
**Six marriages, the register closed on 31 December 1812, and the Zanelli–Roder promise is not among them.**

Eleven images. **Act N. 5**, Thursday 17 September: *Steffani*, a shoemaker of Luincis, thirty, with *Osvalda Corva* of Muina. **Act N. 6**, Monday 28 December: *Steffani Lorenzo*, twenty-nine, villico of Ovasta. **Act N. 4**, 22 July. Acts **1–3** read at page level only — Bressan, Poli, Nino, Vidoni, Fabris, Roder, Gortan, Della Pietra, Micoli.

Then: *«Li 31 trent'uno del mese di Decembre anno mille ottocento dodeci — Il sottoscritto Ufficiale dello Stato Civile della Comune di Mione dichiara chiuso il presente Registro.»*

**Nor is the couple in the 1813 or 1814 alphabetical tables.**

**This matters because of what the series is called.** The 1806 title leaf reads *«Registro per l'esposizione delle pubblicazioni matrimoniali, e per le **opposizioni**»* — publications **and oppositions**. A banns notice invites the world to object. Most are followed by a wedding; some are not.

**It does not touch the Ottavia finding**, which rests on the notices themselves: she and her parents are named there by a public official whose job was to get the filiation right.

*Three of the six acts are still untranscribed, and the 1814 table's left column is partly lost in the binding shadow. Probably not married at Mione in 1812–14; not certainly.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Nati» 1808, act N. 16 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The birth registers, finally located — and the first volume opened
rows.got:
**A sister nobody had, and a child nobody had, in four lines.**

**Sunday 10 July 1808.** *«Si è presentata al sottoscritto Ufficiale dello Stato Civile **de' Franceschi Margherita**, dell'età **d'anni ventidue**, domiciliata nel villaggio di Mione, villica di professione, portando seco un Infante di sesso femmineo nato il giorno suddetto alle ore otto di mattina … a cui fu imposto il nome di **Cattarina**. La suddetta Margherita ha pure dichiarato, che la neonata è figlia di **suo fratello Osvaldo de' Franceschi** di professione **Fallegname**, e di **Cattarina nata Prencis** di lui consorte.»*

**Margherita is a fourth sibling and the first one that needs no argument.** Francesco and Osvaldo are called brothers outright in 1809; Giacoma was added to them by inference. Margherita stands in front of the registrar and says whose sister she is. Twenty-two in 1808 → born about **1786**, between Francesco and Osvaldo.

**Cattarina, born 10 July 1808 at eight in the morning**, is a new child — the carpenter's elder daughter, registered the same day she was born.

**Witnesses: Micoli-Toscano Gio: Batta**, twenty-one, of Mione, and Lupieri Valentino, thirty, of Luint. **She could not write** and made her mark.

**And the birth series is located at last: arks an_ua667570–667573, being 1806, 1808, 1809 and 1810 — and nothing after.** The ark space above is empty, checked twice, while marriages, allegati, banns and deaths all run to 1815. **Only the births stop, and they stop in 1810.**

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Nati» 1808, act N. 22 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The second De Franceschi entry in the 1808 birth register — and a check on my own method
rows.got:
**Gio: Pietro Erman de Franceschi carries a newborn into the town hall, and signs for it.**

**Sunday 21 August 1808.** *«Si è presentato … **Erman de' Franceschi G. Pietro, d'anni cinquanta otto**, domiciliato in Mione, di professione agricoltore, portando seco un infante di sesso mascolino, nato il giorno di ieri venti … a cui fu imposto il nome di **Gio: Batta Benedetto**. … esser il neonato figlio di **Pietro Ermanni, e di Orsola nata Crosilla** jugali.»* Witnesses **Lupieri Gio: Batta, thirty-two, «medico di professione»**, and Lupieri Valentino, thirty, both of Luint.

**A new household** — Pietro Ermanni × Orsola née Crosilla of Mione — and **a new child**, born 20 August 1808 at three in the afternoon. The relationship to the notificante is *not stated*; a man of fifty-six carrying a newborn is most naturally the grandfather, and Gio: Pietro's own father was a Pietro Erman, so the child is probably his son's. **Inferred, and labelled so.**

**And it marks down one of my own arguments.** Against his documented birth of 28 April 1752, Gio: Pietro is recorded as **55** (April 1808), **58** (August 1808), **56** (February 1809) and **59** (August 1812) — when he was 56, 56, 56 and 60. **Four months after being called fifty-five he is called fifty-eight.** Yesterday I leaned on age-consistency to identify the Muina Osvaldo and called it the convincing part; on this evidence register ages scatter ±2 and that leg is worth less than I claimed. The identification stands on village and trade.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Nati» 1809, act N. 4 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The 1809 birth register re-read for notificanti and witnesses, not only parents
rows.got:
**A household nobody had, headed by a man with the deepest name in the file.**

**Thursday 2 March 1809.** *«Si è presentato … **Maria figlia di Matteo de Franceschi, d'anni dieci otto circa**, domiciliata nel Villaggio di Mione, villica di condizione, portando seco un Infante di sesso femminile nato il giorno d'oggi alle ore due antimeridiane … alla quale furono imposti i nomi di **Giovanna-Maddalena**. … essere la neonata figlia di **Matteo de Franceschi di professione Calzolajo, e di Anna nata Fasiol** sua moglie.»* Witnesses **Valentino Lupieri**, thirty-one, possidente, and **Gio: Battista Roter**, twenty-four, **also a calzolajo**, both of Luint.

**Two Matteos, not one.** Orsola's baptismal extract calls her father *«Pietro quondam Matteo»* — an elder Matteo dead before 1809, born about the 1710s. This one is alive, a shoemaker, with a daughter of eighteen. **The name is being reused a generation and a half later**, and this archive is not welding them.

**A fifth trade** for the surname at Mione: tailor, carpenter, farmer, landowner, and now *calzolajo*.

**And the clerk's own word for the daughter:** *«Notificante de Deffranceschi Maria **illetterata** fa il segno di croce»* — not the ordinary *«per non saper scrivere»*. Quoted rather than softened.

**The birth count was understated.** This archive said the 1806–1810 birth index *«opens on three De Franceschi entries»*; those were the first three lines. With Cattarina (1808) and Giovanna-Maddalena (1809) the true figure is **at least five** — and the birth index itself is still not located: the three-page tables at an_ua667540 and an_ua667566 are the **marriage** and **death** indexes.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Nati» 1809, act N. 15 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Gio: Pietro Erman de Franceschi as a witness — and what his title says about the year of his second marriage
rows.got:
**«Ambi possidenti» — and it dates a change of station to within five months.**

**Sunday 9 July 1809.** Maria Ortis, thirty-four, *illetterata*, of Muina, brings in a girl born the previous day at one in the morning, **Lucia Lauretana**, daughter of Filippo Ortis and Margherita née Sottardi. The witnesses are *«**Erman de Franceschi Gio: Pietro** d'anni **cinquantaquattro circa** e **Gio: Pietro Giorgi** d'anni cinquantotto, **ambi possidenti**, domiciliati nel villaggio di Mione»*.

**He is already a landowner in July 1809.** The marriage act of **13 February 1809** still calls him *agricoltore*; so does every act before it. **Five months, and the word changes** — which is a much tighter bracket than the 1812 death act gave, and it sits squarely after his marriage to Orsola de Franceschi.

**And his age goes the wrong way again.** Born 28 April 1752, he was **fifty-seven** that day and the register says **fifty-four circa**. The run is now 55, 58, 56, **54**, 59 for a man who was 56, 56, 56, 57, 60 — a spread of five years. Any argument of mine that leans on register ages should be discounted accordingly, and the Muina Osvaldo identification has been re-graded to rest on village and trade.
ev: The Erman man, a class up

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Nati» 1810, acts N. 1 and N. 21 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: The last surviving birth register, read for notificanti and witnesses as well as parents
rows.got:
**Two acts, and the second of them proves my own method wrong.**

**Act N. 1, Sunday 14 January 1810.** *«**Francesco de' Franceschi, d'anni ventisei circa, di professione Sarto**, portando seco un infante di sesso feminile nato il giorno d'oggi **alle ore tre antimeridiane** … **Anna Cecilia**»* — his daughter by **Margherita nata Gortan**. Witnesses Antonio Bressan, twenty-six, *domestico*, and Matteo Lupieri, *possidente*, of Luint. He signs. **The child is dead on 25 January, eleven days old** — the death act guesses *«un mese circa»*.

**Act N. 21, Thursday 15 October 1810.** *«**de Franceschi Osvaldo, d'anni ventisei**, di professione **fa legname** … nato il giorno d'oggi **alle ore dieci antimeridiane** … **Gio: Batta**»*, his son by **Cattarina nata Crencis**, *«fa legname il primo, agricoltrice la seconda»*. Witnesses **Roter Gio: Batta, twenty-four, calzolajo** and **Brovedan Pietro, twenty-seven, sarto**, both of **Luint**.

**The signature is the finding.** In January 1809 Osvaldo signed *«Osvaldo Ant.o De Franceschi»* — upright, capitalised, practised. Here, twenty-one months later, he signs *«**de franceski osualdo**»* — lower-case, surname first, *Franceschi* as *franceski*, his own forename as *osualdo*. **One man, two hands so different that in separate parishes I would have called them two people.** Three days ago I compared two signatures and leaned on the likeness; I withdrew that yesterday on other grounds. This is the demonstration that the withdrawal was right, and it comes from the man himself.

**And the wife's surname will not hold still**: **Brenci** (1806 Morti), **Prencis** (1808 Nati, a clear P), **Crencis** (this act), **Brenis** (1812 banns), **Brunis** (1815 banns). This archive has tried three times to settle it and now records all the forms with their acts and prefers none.

**The 1810 «twenty-six» outlier is real** — read off the act, reported by the father in person. Ages here are worth about three years either way.

*With Gio: Batta the civil births stop. Anything born to these households 1811–1815 is in the Pieve di Gorto or nowhere.*

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Ovaro, «Matrimoni» 1815 (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Felice Santo de Franceschi's marriage act, predicted to be at Ovaro because the bride was of Liariis
rows.got:
**It was where the Code said it would be, and it carries a word this archive has never had.**

**«Registro Matrimonj, Anno 1815, Comune di Ovaro»** — ark an_ua679991, five leaves. **Thursday 15 June 1815, five in the afternoon.** Banns on two Sundays, 28 May and 4 June; the second is the Mione notice already published here.

> *«…sono comparsi per contrarre matrimonio **Felice Santo de Franceschi, di professione tessitore, d'anni ventidue compiti**, nato, e domiciliato in **Mione** … **figlio di Paolo de Franceschi di professione falegname** …, e di **Anna nata Brencis** di condizione villica … e **Lucia Santa de Canova d'anni ventitré**…»*

**A weaver.** The 1679 headmen's return that opens this archive is a return of **weavers** — *«compaiono soltanto i tessitori recatisi nella contea di Pisino»* — and it names *«Zuane De Franceschi con un suo fiolo»* of Mione. This archive has held tailors, a carpenter, farmers, a landowner and a shoemaker of the surname; **it has never held a weaver.** Now it does, in the same village, 136 years later. It proves no descent and is not offered as one.

**But the Mione banns of 4 June call the same man «Sartore».** Two clerks, eleven days, two cloth trades. That weakens the weaver finding *and* the tailor argument this page has leaned on; what survives is that the family worked cloth.

**And Anna's surname is written «Brencis» here** — the form already held for Cattarina, the carpenter's wife. After six spellings across five acts I had written that the two women were «two clusters that may join»; a second comune joins them.

**Witnesses**, all of Liariis, all with their fathers named: Giovanni del fu Giacomo Crisilla (69, possidente) · Daniele del fu Osvaldo de Canova (49, possidente) · Giacomo del fu Nicolò Crisilla (69, falegname) · Giovanni di Nicolò Sabina (27). **He signed; the bride «dichiara essere illetterata».**

*One oddity left open: Daniele «del fu Osvaldo» de Canova stands at the wedding of a bride «figlia del fu Osvaldo Antonio» de Canova, and the act calls all four witnesses «non parenti, né affini». Either two dead Osvaldos at Liariis, or the formula is boilerplate. The Ovaro 1815 allegati would say.*
ev: The banns that sent me there

rows.src: Matricula Online (data.matricula-online.eu) — the whole portal
rows.what: Whether Senj and Karlobag, and any Croatian parish at all, are on Matricula — the plan said they were
rows.got:
**Croatia is not on Matricula. Not Senj, not Karlobag, not one parish.**

The portal's own fonds index lists exactly twelve countries — **Germany, Austria, Poland, Serbia, Luxembourg, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Slovenia, Italy, Switzerland** and three private collections. There is no Croatian section. Its place search returns **nothing** for *Senj*, *Karlobag*, *Rijeka* or *Fiume*.

**This archive's own plan said otherwise.** Matricula was written down as a fifth provider *«(Senj, Karlobag)«* and scheduled for building into the research map. That was an assumption never checked, and it was wrong. It is struck from the plan rather than quietly dropped.

**One thing there is worth keeping**: searching *Trieste* returns two Austrian Protestant congregations — **Triest AB** and **Triest HB** — under the Evangelical section. Not Croatian, not Catholic, and no De Franceschi is known in either; but Trieste Evangelical registers are a shelf this archive has never looked at, and the family was in the Littoral.
rows.dest: Matricula Online — fonds index and place search
ev: The research map, which now has four providers and not five

rows.src: ARHiNET (arhinet.arhiv.hr), the Croatian state archives' own network
rows.what: Retried as a possible provider for the research map
rows.got:
**Still does not resolve.** Neither `https://arhinet.arhiv.hr/` nor the plain-HTTP form answers at all — not a 403, not a redirect, no connection. `ara.arhiv.hr` is the same.

This is the second time this archive has tried ARHiNET and the second time it has recorded nothing. **Pazin's own list stays the only Croatian archive catalogue in the research map**, and it is the only source in it that admits which volumes are not digitised anywhere.

rows.src: Portale Antenati — the Udine inventory for Mione and Ovaro, catalogued rather than read
rows.what: Every civil-register volume for the two comuni, turned into an addressable list
rows.got:
**Fifty-nine volumes, each one openable, none of them indexed by name.**

Mione's Napoleonic and Austrian civil registration runs in seven series — **Matrimoni** (9 volumes), **Matrimoni allegati** (13), **Matrimoni indici** (3), **Pubblicazioni** (9), **Morti** (9), **Morti indici** (3) and **Nati** (4). Ovaro adds a **Matrimoni** run of nine.

**The shape of that list is itself the finding.** Deaths and marriages run nine volumes; births run four. The civil births stop at 1810 while everything else carries on to 1815 — and 1807 is absent from every series. Anyone born into these households between 1811 and 1815 is in the **Pieve di Gorto** or nowhere.

**Years are given only where an act fixes them.** Four of the Nati are dated exactly, and two Ovaro Matrimoni are; the rest are numbered within their series and given the series span, because that is what the inventory supports.
rows.dest: Antenati, Archivio di Stato di Udine
ev: All fifty-nine, every one a link

rows.src: Portale Antenati — the Mione inventory, walked ark by ark (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Forty-six catalogue pages fetched one at a time, to fix which comune, series and year each ark actually is
rows.got:
**The inference held, and the assumption behind it did not.**

Mione's marriages, allegati, indices and banns came back exactly as this archive had predicted from the ranges: **Matrimoni 1806, 1808–1815 (9) · Pubblicazioni, the same nine years · Matrimoni allegati, 13 across those years with two apiece for 1808–1811 · Matrimoni indici, three only — 1806–1810, 1811, 1812, and then nothing.** Every series missing 1807.

**But the very first ark fetched was not Mione.** `an_ua667510` is **Mieli, in the Comune di Comeglians** — Morti 1807 — and 667512 and 667513 are Mieli's Nati for 1806 and 1807. The portal does not number one comune per block, and an Ovaro range this archive had claimed on that assumption is withdrawn.

**Antenati stops answering after about forty-six pages.** Every request after that returns **HTTP 400**, including arks already fetched successfully — a rate limit wearing an error code, not a bad address.

*The catalogue now records how each volume's identity is known* — walked, read, or unconfirmed — and five arks inside Mione's range are left unconfirmed rather than given a year they might not have.
ev: The catalogue, every ark a link

rows.src: Portale Antenati — the Ovaro inventory, walked ark by ark (Archivio di Stato di Udine)
rows.what: Whether Ovaro's civil registers have the 1807 that Mione is missing
rows.got:
**They do. Ovaro's marriages run 1806 to 1815 without a single gap** — ark an_ua679982 through an_ua679991, ten volumes, and **1807 is an_ua679983**.

**Only the marriages are digitised at Ovaro**: no births, no deaths, no banns. The **allegati** run eight volumes (an_ua679993–680000) and are missing 1806 and 1809; the **indices** are two, 1806–1810 and 1811.

**This is the correction that matters.** This archive had written, twice, that 1807 was absent from both comuni. It is absent from **Mione**. The next comune up the valley kept it — so 1807 is not a year the system failed, it is **one lost Mione volume**, and that is a question an archivist can answer.

**And it points at a cheaper route than a letter.** The Mione index says Osvaldo Defranceschi married Valentina Prencis on 6 August 1807. The Ovaro 1807 allegati exist and cost nothing to open.

*The 400 errors that stopped the first Antenati walk were never a rate limit.* The portal writes a «recently viewed» entry into the cookie for every register opened; at about 8 KB the Cookie header exceeds Apache's limit and the server answers *«Size of a request header field exceeds server limit»*. **Fetching with credentials omitted returns 200 immediately.** Forty-six pages of throttling that was not throttling.
ev: All seventy-four volumes, every one a link
What survives and what does not

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Ovaro, «Matrimoni, allegati» 1815 (Archivio di Stato di Udine), ark an_ua680000
rows.what: Felice Santo de Franceschi's proof of birth, demanded by the Code before the registrar would marry him
rows.got:
**It names his grandfather, and the archive did not have one.**

*«**Die 2 9mbris 1792.** Sanctus = Felix filius leg. ac naturalis **Pauli filii Petri De Franceschi mionensis**, et Annae, jugalium. Heri … est ad lucem, et hodie solemniter baptizatus fuit a me Joannem Baptistam Darium P.M. in Ecclesia Parochiali Plebana.»*

**Pietro De Franceschi of Mione** — Paolo's father. The extract is the Pieve di Santa Maria di Gorto's own baptismal register, copied out and certified by the priest who held it at **Luincis on 14 June 1815**, because the Napoleonic Code would not marry a man without proof of birth and Mione had no civil register before 1806. **A page of the book this archive has been trying to reach for two days has come to us inside a civil marriage file.**

**Godfather: «Domino Joanne quondam Floreani Micoli = Toscano»** — a Micoli Toscano, the family whose Mione palace holds the 1679 weavers' contracts. **Godmother: «Domina Magdalena filia quondam Joannis Prencis»**, both of Mione — the P-form of the surname, in a priest's Latin, in 1792.

**Also in the file:** Lucia Santa de Canova's own extract — born **12 May 1793 at the fourteenth hour**, daughter of Osvaldo Antonio De Caneva and Lucia Colinassio, baptised at S. Vigilio; and her consent act of 14 June 1815 before her widowed mother, which calls Paolo **«il vivente Paolo de Franceschi»** — alive — and **«possidente»**, where the marriage act eleven days later calls him a carpenter.

*Born 12 May 1793 she was twenty-two at the wedding, not the twenty-three the act gives.* Four images of the eleven belong to a different couple entirely, the Fedele–Solari wedding of Clavais.
ev: The six spellings, and the P-form
The wedding it was filed for

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Morti» 1810, acts N. 1 to N. 5 (Archivio di Stato di Udine), ark an_ua667557
rows.what: The first of the nine Mione death registers to be read end to end, looking for a Pietro De Franceschi
rows.got:
**No Pietro. But the first act on the first page corrects this archive twice.**

*«Comune di Mione **li 25 Venticinque Gennajo** mille ottocento dieci … ove ha riconosciuto il cadavere di **De Franceschi Anna Cecilia** morta questo giorno alle ore otto pomeridiane **in età di un Mese c.a**»* — witnesses **Bressan Antonio**, twenty-six, *domestico*, and **Lupieri Matteo**, twenty-two, *possidente*, both of **Luint**, who declare her born at Mione to **Francesco de Franceschi** and **Margherita nata Gortan**, *«di professione sarto il primo, agricoltrice la seconda»*.

**She died on the 25th, not the 28th** — the date is written in figures and spelled out, agreeing. **And she was eleven days old, not a month**: the birth act four images away in the Nati of the same year has her born **Sunday 14 January 1810 at three in the morning**, presented by the same father before the same two witnesses.

**Giacomo Micoli wrote both acts and guessed the age of a child whose birth he had himself recorded.** This archive believed the guess, built a December 1809 birth on it, and then kept the wrong death date even after finding the real birth. [Logged](/corrections/).

*The rest of the volume, so far:* act N. 4 is **Mario Catterina** of Entrampo, 2 March 1810, aged seventy-five, daughter of Mario Giacomo and Catterina nata Roder. No De Franceschi in acts 2 to 5.
ev: The birth, and the eleven days

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Ovaro, «Matrimoni, allegati» 1807 (Archivio di Stato di Udine), ark an_ua679993
rows.what: Opened on the chance that a Mione couple's 1807 papers had been filed at Ovaro, Mione's own volume being lost
rows.got:
**No De Franceschi. But the file is not Carnian — it came up from Istria.**

Seven images, one marriage. The banns were published **at Capodistria and at Covedo** on **17 and 24 May 1807**; the groom's widowed mother notarised her consent **at Capodistria on 28 May**; a second consent was taken **at Ovaro** by *«Osvaldo Machin quondam Pietro, Notaio residente nel Comune d'Osais»*; and the seventh image is **the letter itself, still folded**, addressed *«All'Ufficiale dello Stato Civile della Comune d'Ovaro»* and endorsed on the diagonal *«L'Ufficiale dello Stato Civile di Capodistria»*.

**The groom is a «sarto».** A tailor, marrying between Istria and the Val di Gorto, in 1807.

**This archive's road, running the other way, on paper.** Everything held for the Carnia-to-Istria migration until now has been Istrian-side — a 1679 list quoted in a book, a surname in a Gračišće register. Here are two civil offices in two provinces corresponding about one wedding.

**And it changes what the thirteen unread Mione allegati are worth.** An allegato is where out-of-town paper lands. One of them already [gave this archive Pietro De Franceschi](/carnia/#allegati1815) out of the Pieve di Gorto's lost register; this one proves the same series can hold **Istrian** documents. A Mione man who had gone down to Istria and come home to marry would leave his papers exactly here.

*The surnames are not published.* The hand is a fast notarial cursive on a photograph of a photograph; the groom reads plausibly as **Sorj** or **Sorsi** and the bride as **Ellero**, daughter of Michiel, her mother a **Dolfen** — and none of that is firm enough to assert. The dates, places, trades and offices are.
ev: The file, and what it implies
The allegato that gave up a grandfather
Why 1807 was worth trying at all

rows.src: Portale Antenati — Mione, «Matrimoni, allegati» 1806 (Archivio di Stato di Udine), ark an_ua667526
rows.what: The first of Mione's thirteen allegati volumes, opened because two others had already given up a generation apiece
rows.got:
**Two generations in one sheet.**

*«Certifico io sottoscritto Parroco della **Pieve Matrice di Gorto a parte Luvincis**, come **Giacoma** figlia legitima, e naturale di **Osvaldo quondam Gio: Batta De' Franceschi di Mione**, e di **Cattarina** sua moglie, essa è nata li **25 del mese di Maggio nell'anno 1789**, come consta dal Libro dei Battezzi. In fede. Da Luvincis li 5 del mese d'Agosto 1806. D. **Gio: Batta Dario** R.do, manu propria sigillo munivi.»* **The paper seal is still on the sheet**, and under it the **Sindaco of Mione** certifies on 30 August that the extract is in Dario's own hand.

**Gio: Batta De' Franceschi**, dead before 1789 · **Osvaldo**, his son, dead before 1806 · **Giacoma**, born 25 May 1789. Copied by the priest who held the book — the same Don Dario who copied [Felice Santo's extract](/carnia/#allegati1815) nine years later. **Two pages of a register nobody can open, delivered by the Napoleonic bureaucracy.**

**The marriage is to Ignazio di Prato of Chialina**, baptised 13 December 1777 *«natus hac nocte praeterita»*, son of Giacomo son of the late **Leonardo de Prato** and of Cattarina, godparents Gio: Batta de Prato and Marianna daughter of Antonio Durigussi, signed **D. Io: Bapta de Benedictis, Vicarius**. His widowed mother consented before a notary at Chialina on 8 September 1806.

**And the trap is flagged rather than walked into.** This Osvaldo is **not** the Osvaldo *«fa legname»* this archive already holds — a carpenter aged twenty-six in 1810, alive and signing through 1815, also married to a Cattarina. Giacoma was born when he was five. **Two men of one name in one village, recorded as two.**

*And it documents somebody the family tree already knew.* A **Giacoma Defranceschi (di Prato)** has sat in the roster since the MyHeritage import with no source and no dates. She now has both.
ev: The extract, and the two generations
The other grandfather, nine years later
The Ovaro file that came up from Istria

rows.src: FamilySearch — the whole catalogue of 3,488 historical record collections
rows.what: Whether Croatian places are filmed in collections filed under other countries, and what this archive's map cannot see
rows.got:
**They are, and the clearest case is a whole Croatian county.**

*«Slovenia, Prekmurje and Međimurje, Civil Registers, 1895–1918»* (cc 1985107) browses under two roots — **Vas** and **Zala**, Hungarian counties. Under Zala are **33 registration districts**, and nearly every one is a Croatian town: **Csáktornya** is Čakovec, **Perlak** is Prelog, **Nedelicz** is Nedelišće, **Stridó** is Štrigova, **Kottori** is Kotoriba, **Légrád** is Legrad. A Croatian county's civil registers, under Hungarian place names, in a collection named for Slovenia. **None of them is on this archive's map.**

*«Italy, Pola and Trieste, Catholic Church Records, 1593–1941»* (cc 2152685) holds seven Istrian parishes under «Pola» — **Buie, Cittanova d'Istria, Portole, Verteneglio, Materada, Isola d'Istria, Pirano**. **Five are in Croatia today** — Buje, Novigrad, Oprtalj, Brtonigla, Materada. Not our parishes, but the same mechanism.

*«Croatia, Delnice Deanery Catholic Church Books, 1571–1926»* (cc 1875189) is a **second Croatian church-book collection** this archive did not know existed — the Gorski kotar deanery inland from Crikvenica. **It browses by film number, not by parish**, which is why a place-based walk never found it.

**Ruled out**, so they need not be checked again: Trieste's two civil-registration collections (Duino, Muggia, Sgonico, Trieste, and one root called «Slovenia») and the Gorizia census, which has no browse tree at all.

**Untested and most promising: «Austria, Catholic Church Records, 1565–2007»** — the Austrian Littoral governed Istria and the Kvarner until 1918, and it is the likeliest hiding place for **Gračišće, Gologorica and Pićan**, which FamilySearch's Croatian collection does not hold at all. And **«Hungary, Civil Registration, 1895–1980»**, for Fiume and the Hungarian littoral.

*Method note:* `/platform/records/collections/<cc>/waypoints` opens the browse tree of **any** collection, not just 2040054. That is how each of these was opened.
ev: The ten collections, and what is in each
The map, and what it cannot see

rows.src: FamilySearch — collections 2152685, 1985107 and 1875189, walked and merged into the research map
rows.what: Putting Croatian places that are filed under Italy and Slovenia onto the same dots as their modern names
rows.got:
**58 places, 409 volumes, 32 of the places in Croatia — and a four-year hole that nobody could have seen before.**

**Čakovec** now carries two collections on one marker: *Croatia, Church Books* (parish registers to 1890) and *Slovenia, Prekmurje and Međimurje* (Hungarian civil registration from 1895), the second filed under **«Csáktornya»**. Put side by side, the timeline reads:

**Births 1748–1906, in 2 stretches · GAP 1891–1894 · Marriages the same · Deaths the same.**

**Four years, in all three record types, in a county town.** That is the interval between the church books closing and Hungarian civil registration opening — and it was invisible while the two collections sat in different countries' catalogues.

**The exonym table is the whole trick.** Csáktornya→Čakovec, Perlak→Prelog, Nedelicz→Nedelišće, Stridó→Štrigova, Kottori→Kotoriba, Légrád→Legrad, Buie→Buje, Cittanova d'Istria→Novigrad, Portole→Oprtalj, Verteneglio→Brtonigla. The catalogue's spelling stays in the marker's «also written» line, **because that is the name you have to search for to find the book**.

**Delnice** is honest about its limits: six reels, ~3,485 images, **no parish structure at all**, so they hang on the deanery town rather than pretending to a precision the collection does not have.

*And a second language problem surfaced and was fixed.* Hungarian titles — **Születtek, Házasultak, Halottak** — matched none of the archive's record-type patterns, so 365 volumes fell into «Other» and a whole Croatian county's coverage timeline said nothing. The matcher now reads five languages.
ev: The collections, and what each holds

rows.src: FamilySearch — «Austria, Catholic Church Records, 1565–2007» (collection 5000002)
rows.what: Whether the Austrian Littoral is in it — the most promising place Gračišće, Gologorica and Pićan could be hiding
rows.got:
**It is not. The Littoral is not in this collection, and the hole stays open.**

The collection holds **6.85 million records and 17.4 million persons** and has **no browse tree at all** — `/platform/records/collections/5000002/waypoints` returns 404, because it is a name index rather than a filmed set. So it was searched instead.

**289 Defranceschi records inside it**, pulled in full. Every named place among the 393 fact-rows is Tyrolean or Upper Austrian: **Bozen, Salorno (Tirolo), Tyrol, St. Florian bei Linz**. **Not one in Istria, Gorizia, Trieste or Fiume.** Three Istrian surnames tested beside it fall the same way — **Sestan** at Zwettl, Longomosso and Feldkirch; **Kostesich** at Bozen; **Miškulin** at Bozen.

*The filter was verified rather than trusted.* Defranceschi returns **303,320** with no collection filter, **289** with `f.collectionId=5000002`, **3,550** with the Croatian collection, and **0** with a made-up collection id. The control says the filter bites.

**Two things worth keeping.**

**There is a Tyrolean Defranceschi population** — 289 records clustered on **Bozen and Salorno**, South Tyrol. A separate family of the same surname, several hundred kilometres from Carnia, and a standing argument against ever reasoning from the name alone.

**And Slavonia does appear**: one record reads *«Vukovar, Sriem, Croatia, Austria»*. So the collection reaches into Croatia-Slavonia even though it does not reach the coast.
ev: The ten collections, and what each holds
The three parishes still filmed nowhere

rows.src: FamilySearch — «Hungary, Civil Registration, 1895–1980» (collection 1452460)
rows.what: Whether Fiume, the Croatian littoral or Međimurje are in it — the last of the promising candidates
rows.got:
**No. And the reason is constitutional, which makes this a better answer than a hit would have been.**

The collection browses by **33 Hungarian counties** — Abaúj-Torna, Arad, Bács-Bodrog, Baranya, Bars, Békés … Vas, Veszprém, Zala. **Not one Croatian-Slavonian county** — no Zagreb, no Varaždin, no Modruš-Rijeka, no Lika-Krbava, no Srijem — **and no Fiume**, despite Fiume being a Hungarian *corpus separatum*.

**Hungary introduced civil registration in 1895. Croatia-Slavonia did not.** Under the Nagodba it ran its own administration and **kept the parish registers as the legal civil record until 1946**. That single fact explains why FamilySearch's Croatian collection is *church books* and why **there is no Croatian civil registration to find anywhere** — it was never created.

**And it explains Međimurje.** [Međimurje's civil registers exist from 1895](/elsewhere/) because Međimurje was administered as part of **Zala county — as Hungary proper, not as Croatia**. The anomaly was never an archival quirk; it was a border.

*Checked rather than assumed.* Zala in this collection holds **235 districts** and not one of **Csáktornya, Perlak, Nedelicz, Stridó, Kottori or Légrád** — those sit in the Slovenia-titled collection, so the two do not overlap and nothing is duplicated. The **16 Defranceschi** records inside are **Budapest, Esztergom and Sopron**.

**Both promising candidates are now closed.** Gračišće, Gologorica and Pićan are not in Austria and not in Hungary, and on present evidence **they are filmed nowhere**.
ev: The collections, and what each holds
What Pazin holds on paper instead

rows.src: FamilySearch — all 3,488 historical record collections, walked to exhaustion
rows.what: Every collection that could hold a record for this family's ground, opened through its browse tree or searched inside
rows.got:
**Forty-four opened. Five hold our ground. Thirty-nine hold nothing, and that is now written down so nobody opens them again.**

**The five**: *Croatia, Church Books* · *Croatia, Delnice Deanery* · *Italy, Pola and Trieste* · *Slovenia, Prekmurje and Međimurje* · *Italy, Udine*. **All five are on the map.**

**What is not there at all: no Serbian, Bosnian, Montenegrin or Yugoslav collection exists** — not one in 3,488 — so the Dalmatian hinterland has no coverage from that direction. **And Croatia itself has exactly two collections.**

**Austria and Hungary both came back empty, and between them they explain why.** Hungary registered civilly from 1895 and Croatia-Slavonia did not, keeping the parish books as the legal record until 1946; Austria's collection is a name index of the Alpine dioceses, not of a Littoral that stopped being Austrian in 1918. **Gračišće, Gologorica and Pićan are filmed nowhere at all.**

**One near-miss checked and closed**: *Italy, Venezia, Civil Registration 1806–1817* has a root called **Gorizia** — but its children are **Belvedere, Grado and Isola Morosini**, the Friulian lagoon, not Istria.

**And a warning handed over free.** Defranceschi is a **Veneto** name: **9,626** records at Padova, **6,546** at Venice, **2,076** at Verona, **1,285** at Treviso, **289** in Tyrol. None of them is this family and none can be excluded without a document.

*Method, for whoever does this next:* `/platform/records/collections/<cc>/waypoints` opens the browse tree of **any** collection and `f.collectionId` counts names inside one — two calls per candidate. The filter was verified with a control: the same surname returns **303,320** unfiltered, **289** in Austria, **3,550** in Croatia, **0** against a made-up id.
ev: The five that hold Croatian places
Why Croatia has no civil registration before 1946

rows.src: This archive's own data files, audited against the research map
rows.what: Whether every place-based source the archive has used actually reaches the map
rows.got:
**One did not, and it was the archive's own work.**

`sweep.json` holds a sweep of the **FamilySearch library catalogue** — not the image collections, but the printed editions, transcriptions and microfilms — **by place-authority id across 75 places**, made weeks ago and never wired to anything. **189 items across 61 places, plus 14 places where somebody looked and found nothing.**

It is now the map's seventh provider. Two things changed immediately:

**The «in no catalogue at all» colour went from 3 places to 8**, and five of the new ones — **Grožnjan, Lindar, Motovun, Višnjan, Villa Santina** — are *checked* negatives rather than blanks. A place somebody looked at and found nothing for is worth more than a place nobody opened.

**Cross-checked places went from 27 to 83**, which is what makes gap detection possible at all — a gap can only be seen where two catalogues describe the same place.

*And a language fix fell out of it*: the catalogue's titles are Croatian — «Matična knjiga **krštenih**» — which matched none of the record-type patterns, so Umag's baptisms were filed under «Other».

**What is deliberately not on the map**: the person-level indexes (FamilySearch record hits, the Austrian index), the newspapers, the DNA, the books, and the 50 diaspora cemeteries in `graves.json`. Those are not record-book holdings and a map of shelves is the wrong shape for them.
ev: The 83 sources, now driven by the register

rows.src: Findmypast — one-month full subscription, four spellings
rows.what: The whole surname paged out again with no clock on it: defranceschi, de franceschi, defranceski, de franceski
rows.got: **644 distinct records in 44 record sets** — six sets more than the two trials could see. **424 pass this archive's rule for publication**; 220 are counted and published nowhere, being the electoral registers, the Social Security Death Index, the obituary notices and the divorce indexes, which is where the living are. [The whole sweep](/findmypast/).

rows.src: Findmypast — «defraneski»
rows.what: A spelling the roster carries, tried against the whole of Findmypast
rows.got: **Zero results.** A checked negative: the spelling exists in this family's own records and Findmypast indexes nobody under it.

rows.src: Findmypast — Wales Roman Catholic Marriages
rows.what: A record set no earlier pass had opened
rows.got: **Emerico De Franceschi married Mariettam Cosulich at St Peter's, Roath, Cardiff, on 26 July 1876** — his father Francisci, hers Josephi Francisci Cosulich, in the priest's Latin. **Cosulich is a Lussino and Trieste shipowning family**, and Cardiff in 1876 is where the Adriatic sailing fleet loaded coal. The first record of the name in Wales. [What it opens](/findmypast/).

rows.src: Findmypast — Italy Births & Baptisms, Marriages, Deaths & Burials 1806–1900
rows.what: Three Italian parish sets, opened for the first time, and their transcripts read
rows.got: Ten records of the name, and **every transcript puts them at Napoli or Vicenza** — two brothers baptised at San Marco di Palazzo, Napoli in 1842 and 1844 to Carmine de Franceschi and Angiola Conti; a Valentino Mario and a Lucia Caterina born at Vicenza in 1900; a Domenico of Vicenza, 1829–1900. **Not Istria, not Carnia, not the Kvarner.** Written down so the three sets are not opened again expecting this family.

rows.src: Findmypast — the American censuses, read for place rather than for name
rows.what: Where the 644 records actually sit
rows.got: **A Puerto Rican cluster eleven towns deep** — Isabela 11, San Lorenzo 9, Ponce 7, then Guayama, Lajas, Luquillo, Peñuelas, San Sebastián, Yauco, Ceiba, Pueblo Este. [The live tree cites seven Puerto Rican people of the name](/live-tree/) from the same ground, so two independent sources agree. Nineteenth-century Corsican emigration to Puerto Rico is well documented and [Corsica is already on this site](/corsica/) as a parallel. **A lead, not a relation.**

rows.src: Findmypast — «Cosulich», and «Marietta Cosulich»
rows.what: Whether the Cardiff bride of 1876 is anywhere else, and whether the marriage was registered civilly as well as in the parish
rows.got:
**Marietta Cosulich appears exactly once in the whole of Findmypast** — and it is the second entry for the same wedding, in the **civil** index rather than the Catholic register: *England & Wales Marriages*, **Cardiff district, Glamorganshire, Q3 1876, volume 11A, page 428**, the groom read by the GRO clerk as «Emmerico Defrancrschi». That is an orderable certificate and [an errand](/errands/).

The surname itself is not rare on Findmypast — Cosulichs cross the Atlantic through the 1900s and 1950s, and **Achille Cosulich died in Australia in 1881**, aged thirty. None of them is joined to this marriage yet.

rows.src: Findmypast — the 1920 census at San Lorenzo, Puerto Rico, read in full
rows.what: Whether the Puerto Rican Franceschi are Corsican immigrants or an island family
rows.got:
**An island family, and not ours.** *Cármen Colón de Franceschi*, 23, and *Aurora Cruz de Franceschi*, 25, are both **born in Puerto Rico to parents born in Puerto Rico**, both entered as *esposa*, and both recorded by the enumerator as **Black**. Two generations on the island by 1920 and married into the name rather than born to it.

The surname reached Puerto Rico with the nineteenth-century **Corsican** settlement, which is well documented — but by 1920 it is a Puerto Rican surname. [The thread is closed](/findmypast/).

rows.src: Findmypast — the 1921 Census of England & Wales and the 1939 Register
rows.what: Two collections nobody else holds, against four spellings of the surname
rows.got:
**Nobody of this name is in either.** The 16 September sweep paged out every result for *defranceschi*, *de franceschi*, *defranceski* and *de franceski* — 644 records in 44 record sets — and **neither the 1921 Census nor the 1939 Register is among them**.

Which is a finding, not an absence. The *South Wales Echo* called them **«an old Cardiff family» in 1896**, and [a De Franceschi married a Cosulich there in 1876](/at-sea/). **By 1921 there is no one of the name left in England or Wales at all.** They anglicised, married out, or went back to sea.

rows.src: Findmypast — the Irish, Scottish and English parish collections
rows.what: Every British and Irish parish register set, against four spellings
rows.got:
**One hit in the whole of them, and it is the Cardiff marriage.** Of the 44 record sets the surname touches, the British ones are the civil indexes, the electoral registers, the armed-forces overseas registers, the outward passenger lists — and **Wales Roman Catholic Marriages**, with a single entry.

**No Irish, Scottish or English parish register holds anybody of this name.** For a Catholic family of the Adriatic that is what one would expect; it is written down so that nobody opens them again.

rows.src: Findmypast — the Memphis censuses of 1910, 1930 and 1940, read in full
rows.what: Twenty-one records at one address in Tennessee
rows.got: **A household of eleven.** *Antonio De Franceski*, born **1875 in Italy**, **arrived 1902**, with *Bertha* **born in Germany**, and nine children born 1904–1917. **The 1910 sheet spells them «de Franceski»** — this family's own fused form. Born in Italy in 1875 and leaving in 1902 is the **Carnian** window; Istria in 1875 was Austria and would have been written so. [The reading](/findmypast/).

rows.src: Findmypast — the Chicago household: census, naturalisation index, cemetery
rows.what: Whether the two River Grove burials belong to a family the records can follow
rows.got:
**They do, at every stage.** *Giovanni «John» De Franceschi*, born **1895 in Italy**: head of a Chicago household in the 1930 census with *Freedia* and the children *Thersa* and *Ateo*; **naturalised at Chicago in 1937**, NARA M1285 roll 41; **buried 12 April 1951 at St Joseph's, River Grove**. Frieda died in 1988, and *Attilio F Defranceschi* 1925–2010 is almost certainly Ateo.

**Every one of them says «Italy» and no more.** The petition behind the Soundex index names the comune and [is an errand](/errands/).

rows.src: Findmypast — «Eveline De Franceschi», every collection
rows.what: Whether the Smyrna bride is anywhere else
rows.got: **She appears once in the whole of Findmypast**, and it is the consular marriage itself — GRO MCON, volume 788, line 70, Smyrna, 1906–10. The index does not name the groom; the finder offers **Helen Whittall, Frederick P Wilkinson, Reginald E Turrell** from the same page, and the Whittalls are the Levantine merchant house of Smyrna. **Unresolved**, and [left unresolved](/findmypast/).

rows.src: Findmypast — four naturalisation and passport transcripts, read for the birthplace
rows.what: Whether an American index names the town an emigrant left
rows.got:
**It does not.** *Giovanni* of Chicago, naturalised 1937; *Giovanni* of Connecticut, passport 1922; *Louis*, passport 1919; *Tobias de Franceski*, passport 1922. Every transcript says **«Birth place: Italy»** and stops. Tobias is the only one with a town and only because he was born in the District of Columbia.

**The town is on the image.** Findmypast holds them, and the transcripts carry the NARA rolls that would fetch the same page from Washington — M1490 rolls 1807, 1008 and 1842, and M1285 roll 41. Written down so that nobody harvests eighteen index rows again expecting eighteen birthplaces.

rows.src: The British Newspaper Archive, and Findmypast's own newspaper search
rows.what: «Cosulich» — the Cardiff bride's family, in the shipping columns
rows.got:
**Not searched: both doors are shut.** The British Newspaper Archive puts a **security challenge** in front of results, and Findmypast's newspaper form carries a **reCAPTCHA field**. This archive does not work round bot checks.

The search itself is a good one and is [on the work list for David](/worklist/): *Cosulich* alone, with *Cardiff*, and with *Aquilone*. The 153 articles already read under this family's own name were reached before the check appeared.

rows.src: The four AutoCluster reports, searched for the surname itself
rows.what: Whether any DNA match in any of the four kits carries this family's name
rows.got:
**One, and it is in the father's report alone.** *Gary DeFranceschi of Brooklyn* — already in David's family tree as a Smart Match, and now a blood tie.

**Both male lines meet at Antonius Defranceschi, born 1825 at Gračišće**: David through his son *Josephus* (1863), Gary through his son *Antonius* (1856). Antonius of 1825 is a son of **Giovanni Battista of Gologorica, born 1787, of house 5** — [the spine](/direct-line/), steps two and three.

**Ivan and Gary are third cousins, and the DNA behaves exactly as that predicts**: about seventy centimorgans at that distance, half of it inherited by a son, and Ivan's report has a 40 cM floor. Gary clears it in the father's report and falls below it in David's. [Written up](/dna/#autoclusters).

rows.src: MyHeritage live tree — Gary DeFranceschi's male line, read upward
rows.what: Whether the Brooklyn branch joins this archive's documented descent
rows.got:
**It joins it at the third step.** Gary → Joseph Jordan (1929, Clifton) → **Giuseppe (1892, Gračišće)** → **Antonius (1856, Gračišće)** → **Antonius (1825, Gračišće)** → **Giovanni Battista (1787, Gologorica)**.

**Every man in it is already in this archive's roster**, and three of them are in the spine. Giuseppe of 1892 is one of [the Gračišće Eleven](/the-eleven/); Giovanni Battista of 1787 is the man at **house 5**.

One branch left Gračišće for **Brooklyn**; the other went to Ledenice, then Crikvenica, Senj and Johannesburg. **The paper says they are the same family and the DNA agrees.**

rows.src: Arolsen Archives — all 79 records under DEFRANCESKI, listed
rows.what: Which collections hold this family, and what each one is
rows.got:
**Counted properly for the first time: 79 person records across five collections**, and they are all one family — [the Pfullingen household](/pfullingen/) and the brothers around it.

**3.1.1.1** names in phonetic order — 21 rows, and they are the same seven people under every spelling a clerk could manage: *Lujza / Luiza / Lusza / Luise*, *Petar / Peter*, *Renate / Renata*, *Zdrafko / Zdravko / Ztravko*, *Ursula / Urzula*. **2.1.3.1** «nationality: Yugoslavian» — 13 rows, each with the town: Crikvenica, Fužine, Neuhausen, Urach, Metzingen, Reutlingen. **2.2.2.1 the War Time Card File** — registration cards and **employees' record books** for **Felix, Ivan, Peter and Zdravko**. **2.3.3.1** — seven more, including an **Anton born 20 January 1890**. **3.1.3.2** — the IRO period 1946–1952 and, under its own heading, **«Emigrations in 1949»**.

**Two references worth writing down.** The CM/1 personal file is **3.2.1.1, ref 32110000 058.158** — *«Personal file of DEFRANCESKI, PETAR, born 15 June 1913 in CRIKVENICA **and of further persons**»* — and the tracing case is **6.3.3.2, T/D 349.822**. The archive already had the second. It did not have the first.

rows.src: Arolsen Archives — Ruža, under the spelling the Germans wrote
rows.what: Whether the DP files name Zdravko's wife and where she came from
rows.got:
**They do, and they spell her HRELJEC.** *«DEFRANCESKI · Rose · HRELJEC · Fuzinä / Belnica · 02/13/1922»*, and elsewhere *«Rose · Fuzina · 02/13/1922»*.

So: **born 13 February 1922 at Fužine**, with **Belnica** beside it — which is a hamlet of Fužine. This archive had her as **Ruža Hreljac** with no date. **The German clerk heard Hreljec**, and the [Fužine registers](/worklist/) will settle which. Her death at Horsham in 1996 is already on the site.

rows.src: Arolsen Archives — the War Time Card File, 2.2.2.1
rows.what: Whether the wartime employment records name the brothers
rows.got:
**Four of them: FELIX, JVAN, PETER and KDRAVKO/ZDRACKO.** The collection is *«Registration cards, employees' record books, individual correspondence»* — which is to say **where they were made to work**.

**JVAN is Ivan, born 24 or 25 June 1925 at Crikvenica** — [David's grandfather](/direct-line/), who was nineteen. The archive knew he was in Germany. It did not know there was a card with his name on it.

rows.src: Trove — the Commonwealth of Australia Gazette, naturalisation notices
rows.what: Whether the Gazette confirms NAA B44 without ordering it, and what address it gives
rows.got:
**It confirms it, it dates it, and it finds a third person nobody was looking for.**

· *Commonwealth of Australia Gazette. Periodic*, No. P2, **16 February 1979, page 66**, under **VICTORIA** — *«Defranceski, Roza, 19 Anderson St, Horsham 3400, 21 7 78»* and *«Defranceski, Zdravko, 19 Anderson St, Horsham 3400, 21 7 78»*. **Naturalised 21 July 1978**, at **19 Anderson Street, Horsham** — not Melbourne, which was only where the file was registered.

· *The same series*, No. P8, **25 October 1978, page 303**, under **SOUTH AUSTRALIA** — *«De Franceski, Anton Mario, 7 Calomba Cres, Happy Valley 5159, 15 2 78»*. **The son took the oath five months before his parents, in another state.**

Four spellings searched across every digitised Australian gazette. The only other persons of the name are a **«Defranceski, M.»** in an Avon Products unclaimed-moneys register, NSW 1975 for a 1967 balance, and **«DeFranceschi Bros, 716 Chappie Lane, Broken Hill»**, NSW 1966 — neither placed. [The whole story](/pfullingen/#gazette).

rows.src: David's live tree — the ARGENTINA placeholder pen
rows.what: What is inside the Argentine holding pen, which no page here had opened
rows.got:
**Five households and eight baptisms in Santa Fe province, 1899–1918, and six of the eight were new here.** Twins **Luis and Carmelita Defranceschi Gallucci, 17 January 1915** at San Lorenzo Mártir; **Rosa** 1917 and **Antonia** 1918 at Serodino; **Tomás Defranceschi Martí** 1910; **Antonio Juan de Franceschi Bono** 1899 at San José del Rincón; **Genaro Belardo Defranceschi** 1903 at El Trébol; **Filomena and Jorge Polsino de Franceschi**, both August 1904, at the cathedral of Rosario.

**Why no search had found them**: two surnames in the Spanish manner, the family name in *second* position in three of the five households, and FamilySearch printing the father beside the child — so the entry for Genaro reads *«Genaro Belardo Defranceschi and Antonio Belardo»* and the surname being searched for is in neither half.

Outside the pen, two Istrians. **Joso Defranceski, born 9 January 1906 at Ližnjan, died Buenos Aires 1970** — the first Istrian of the name this project can put in Argentina. And **Rotilio**, whose daughter **Nelida Albina** carries the only Argentine ark ever attached to this family — and whose citation names **Federico Nebbia** where every comparable citation names the father. [The whole pen, read](/diaspora/#argentina).

rows.src: This repository itself — data/parish-by-record-2026-09.txt
rows.what: Whether the forty burials with no parish named could be placed without a new harvest
rows.got:
**All thirty-six of them, and not one needed a search.** The work-list row said the per-record output of the [Istrian sweep](/istria-sweep/) «was never written to disk». **It is on disk** — ninety-three parishes with the 952 FamilySearch persona ids read under each, and only the summary had ever been published.

**Twenty-five joined on name and date. Eleven needed the twin rule**: FamilySearch mints a persona per *role*, so the same burial carries two ids differing **in the last character only** — *6B47-SK44* and *6B47-SK4W* — with every other field identical. Same record, other id, same parish.

**Svetvinčenat 14 · Pula 8 · Draguč 6 · Rovinj 3 · Vrsar 2 · Šterna 2 · Vižinada 1.** Four of those parishes are new to [the register of the dead](/burials/) and to [the map of ground](/graves-map/). Šterna was also sitting on the **Turkish border** — the gazetteer stops at five hundred people and had matched a Sterna in Evros, Greece.

rows.src: This repository itself — an audit of every person-keyed evidence file
rows.what: Whether any file attaching evidence to a person is read by no build script
rows.got:
**One: `site/src/data/valentino.json`.** Written 6 September with the fourteen children of Valentino Defranceschi out of the Fiume register; read by **no script and no page** for eleven days. It was the only file in `site/src/data` that nothing at all referenced.

**Nine people were harmed by it** — five whose pages estimated a birth «about 1749» over an exact date on disk, four who had no page in this archive at all. Chasing it found **eighty-three more** told *«no record stands behind it»* on a page printing their own headstone.

Every other person-keyed file — `burials`, `graves`, `fsrecords`, `register`, `households`, `roster`, `notes/myheritage-key-rows.md` — is read. The three raw harvests `familysearch-inlaws/-migration/-austria.csv` are read by no script, but their people **do** reach the site by name through the register, so nothing is lost there. [The correction](/corrections/) · [the fourteen children](/fiume-1626/#valentino).

rows.src: The National Archives, Kew — Discovery, the whole catalogue
rows.what: The name in nine spellings, the Cardiff thread, and the ship — the first time this archive has ever asked Kew anything
rows.got:
**Seven records of the name in Britain, 1677 to 1934, and none of them was in this archive before.** Discovery is free, needs no key, and answers JSON at `discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/API/search/records?sps.searchQuery=` — David found it; this archive had not looked at Kew once in its life.

· **SP 99/53/290**, 18/28 November 1677 — *«Franceschi to Gio. della Torre and reply»*, in the State Papers for **Venice**.
· **HCA 45/48/2**, 1805 — a prize appeal from the Vice-Admiralty Court of **Minorca**; the captured ship *Amabile*, **master Mark Franceschi**.
· **WO 372/7/142208–142210**, 1914–1920 — three Great War medal cards, catalogued consecutively: **Lorenzo** (Dorsetshire Regiment, Private 20943), **Ernest** (Middlesex Regiment, Private G/57727), **William C.** (Royal Field Artillery, Driver 69431).
· **HO 334/134/4102** and **HO 144/19309**, 1934 — **Lorenzo Franceschi**, from Italy, resident in London, wife **Agnes Elizabeth**, certificate **AZ4102** issued 4 April 1934. The certificate and the Home Office file, for one man.

**A Lorenzo on a 1914–18 medal card and a Lorenzo naturalising out of Italy in London in 1934 may well be one man** — served first, naturalised after. *(inf — two references, not yet joined.)*

**The sweep behind that.** *«Defranceschi»* 0 · *«Defranceski»* 0 · *«De Franceski»* 0 · *«Franceski»* 0 · *«De Francheschi»* 0 · *«De Franceschi»* 3 · *«Dei Franceschi»* 4 · *Franceschi* 19 · *Francesch\** 42 · *Defrance\** 7. Eleven further records are **Franceschin-**, the diminutive and a different surname, filed as adjacent rather than as this name; three are Piero della Francesca, catalogued as *«Piero dei Franceschi»*.

**The Cardiff thread drew a blank in every direction.** *«Emerico De Franceschi»* 0 · *«De Franceschi» AND Cardiff* 0 · *Bujanovich* 0 · *Lacovich* 0 · *Cattarinich* 0 · *Lussinpiccolo* 0.

**And the ship is the lesson.** *Aquilone* returns **501 records and every one is an Admiralty muster for HMS Aquilon**, a Royal Navy ship of the line. The Cardiff barque of December 1877 is not among them.

**The first reading of that was wrong and is retracted before it was ever published.** This log was about to say that merchant shipping is catalogued by ship and year rather than by master. **It is not**: the crew lists in **BT 99** and **BT 400** are catalogued to the individual, and a title from them reads *«Ship: Belgravian; Official number: 98611. William G S Nash; rank/rating, Master; age, 57; place…»* — name, rank, age and place of birth. So a master of this name **would** be findable — and **tested directly, he is not there**. *Franceschi rank rating* **0** · *Defranceschi seaman* **0**, against **827** for *«place of birth, Italy» master*, which shows the index is dense rather than thin. The person-level cataloguing reaches back well before 1915: **BT 99/1302/37 is 1881** and **BT 99/1718/16B is 1891**, both giving name, rating, age and birthplace. The right question is therefore not whether the index reaches people but **whether Kew's sample covers Cardiff in 1876–77**, because most nineteenth-century crew agreements went to Newfoundland and Kew keeps a fraction. **A negative here is a negative in the index, not at Kew**, and the index is better than it first looked. [Britain, on the map of the name](/diaspora/#britain).

rows.src: Archivinformationssystem — the whole Austrian State Archives, searched by name for the first time
rows.what: Whether the ÖStA catalogue names this family — and whether the €45 the Kriegsarchiv quoted would buy anything
rows.got:
**Ninety-nine records, fifty-three of them the name, and the Kriegsarchiv's own bill is answered by its own catalogue.**

The Austrian State Archives publish a field search that is free, needs no account, and searches **Title contains** across every department. Nobody here had ever run it. One query on the stem *Franceschi* returns **99 records: 53 of this name, 46 of the adjacent diminutives** — AVA 19, FHKA 12, HHStA 11, Kriegsarchiv 7, AdR 4.

**The €45 question is settled, and the answer is half a refund.** On 17 September the Kriegsarchiv quoted €45, payable win or lose, for a *Marinepersonensuche* on Julius and Valentin.

· **Valentin needs no search at all.** He is catalogued to the item: **AT-OeStA/KA Marine NMA PA Offiziere und Beamte Akten QL 944 — DEFRANCESCHI, Valentin, Administrations-Assistent**, a naval *Qualifikationsliste*. *«Permission required: Keine · Accessibility: Öffentlich.»* A file you can cite is a **reproduction order**, not a research fee.

· **Julius is not in the catalogue at all** — and the Kriegsarchiv's own FAQ says why: personnel records of navy men **born after 1865** whose *Heimatzuständigkeit* lay outside today's Austria *«verblieben in den jeweiligen Nachfolgestaaten bzw. wurden dorthin abgetreten»*. Julius was born 1879 on the Kvarner. **His file went to Yugoslavia in 1918.** Vienna quoted to look for something its own website says it does not hold.

**Three men of the name this archive had never met.**

· **Johann Defranceschi, born 1833, Geburtsort Gallignana — which is Gračišće**, the parish this family comes out of. A sailor: *Marinediener 4. Klasse* on one card and *1. Klasse* on two others, so the promotion is visible in the catalogue alone. Three files: **MGBBl 2651**, **VerEv Kdi 219**, **VerEv KL-Mardi 76**.

· **Carl «Dragutin» Defranceschi, born 29 July 1883 at Zara, judge at the district court of Šibenik** — personnel file 1909–1918, **AVA Justiz JM Präs. A 134.22**. An Italian and a Croatian forename on one man in one file, which is this archive's whole thesis in miniature.

· **Peter Defranceschi, Ordensverleihung 1918** — **Ritterkreuz, Kriegsdekoration mit Schwert**, HHStA HA OrdK Kartei **3-168**, Geschäftszahl **1732/1918**. The card only; the act itself sits under the Ordenskanzlei files for 1918.

**And a family of Habsburg accountants nobody had counted.** The Hofkammerarchiv holds **Vicenzo** (Kassa 46, 1847), **Anton** (ORH 3412, *Dalmatinische Provinzial-Staatsbuchhaltung in Zara*), **Johann Baptist** and a second **Valentin** (ORH 3777 and 3778, both *Zentralstaatsbuchhaltung in Venedig*). Venice and Zadar, the two ends of the Adriatic, in one office.

*Method, so it can be repeated: `archivinformationssystem.at/feldsuche.aspx` → row 1 «Title» / «contains» / term; set results per page; Search. Searching the stem **Franceschi** catches every in-scope spelling and the diminutives in one pass.*

rows.src: TNA Discovery — where the nineteenth-century crew agreements actually are
rows.what: Whether Kew or Newfoundland holds a Cardiff crew agreement for 1876–77
rows.got:
**Neither, and both, and a third — in stated proportions.** Kew's own series description for **BT 99** calls it *«a **ten per cent sample** of agreements and crew lists … for the years 1861-1938»*. Discovery separately catalogues, as an external holding, *«Registrar General of Shipping and Seamen, crew lists, agreements and official logbooks (**c70% of total**)», 1863-1938*, held by the **Maritime History Archive, Memorial University of Newfoundland**. The remaining fifth sits in **county record offices** — for a Cardiff ship, Glamorgan Archives.

**The key to all three is a number, not a name.** **MF17** at Kew is the microfiche *«Index to location of crew agreements and logbooks of vessels», 1863-1913*, produced by the Newfoundland archive itself and *«arranged according to the **official number** of the vessel, the vessels are not named»*. Every BT 99 piece in the catalogue is likewise titled by official numbers only.

**So the surname will never find a crew list, however dense the index.** The lookup runs ship → official number → MF17 → repository. That makes the **Cardiff marriage certificate of Q3 1876** the hinge: it is the one document that might name Emerico's vessel.

rows.src: Hungaricana — the given name varied sixteen ways, for the first time
rows.what: Whether the Hungarian forms of the forenames find people the German and Italian forms missed
rows.got:
**Sixteen Hungarian forenames, fourteen nils, two hits — and the two explain the fourteen.**

Every sweep this archive had run varied the **surname** and never the **forename**. So sixteen Magyar forms went to Hungaricana as phrases in Hungarian word order, surname first: *Gyula, Antal, János, Bálint, Vincze, Károly, Mihály, József, Miklós, Alajos, Tódor, Lajos, István, Ede* — **all zero**.

**«Defranceschi Ferencz» returns 4** and **«Defranceschi Péter» returns 1.** Which gives the rule: the Hungarian state wrote its *prose* in Hungarian and its *service lists* in German, so **the surname inverts but the forename stays put**. *Ferencz* works only because it is a **spelling** of Franz, not a translation of it.

**The four Ferencz hits include one that is new** — the **Budapesti utasító of 1848**, a Budapest directory, beside the two already-known pension entries for the Fiume harbour master and his orphan daughter.

**And Péter gave a man nobody here had met:** *«beim Husz. Reg. Nr 8 · **Defranceschi Peter Dr** · beim Garnisons-Spitale zu …»*, **Militärschematismus des österreichischen Kaiserthumes für 1867**, p. 647, under *Militär-Parteien*. A **regimental physician** — now the fourteenth name on [the imperial roll](/imperial/) and the second doctor on it.

*The fourteen nils are evidence rather than silence because the control worked: a method that returns four known records for Ferencz is a method whose zeros can be believed.*

rows.src: NSK digitalna — the National and University Library's full text, both spellings
rows.what: What Croatian digitised books and journals say about the name — the search that had stood pending for a week
rows.got:
**The name turns out to have a village it never left, and an inscription nobody here knew about.**

**Svetvinčenat — and the name is the only one that stayed.** *Atti* 48 (2018), the journal of the Centro di ricerche storiche at Rovigno: *«Il cognome **Defranceschi** era stato l'unico ad avere nel **Castello di San Vincenti** una continuità…»* — **the only surname with continuity in the castle of San Vincenti**. And it acted as a body: *«Guidati da **Antonio Defranceschi**, nel **1780** avevano ottenuto l'esonero dal partecipare alla difesa armata»* — **led by Antonio Defranceschi, in 1780 they obtained exemption from armed defence duty.** This archive had never heard of Svetvinčenat.

**A Glagolitic inscription at Gologorica.** Branko Fučić, *Glagoljski natpisi* (JAZU, Zagreb 1982) — the standard corpus — carries: *«Natpis je vjerojatno registriran u **Gologorici**, gdje su **Defranceschi**…»*. **Gologorica is one of this archive's own origin places.**

**The sentence was then walked out of the closed book a phrase at a time** — the full-text index re-centres its snippet on whatever phrase you search, so a copyright-restricted page can be read forwards in steps: *«Riječ »**Pomjane**« (ime istarskog sela) ne može se čitati u posljednjem retku. Natpis je vjerojatno registriran u Gologorici, **gdje su Defranceschi imali posjed i** …»* — *«…where the Defranceschi **had an estate and** …»*

**So it is not a mention, it is a landholding**, and Fučić uses it to date the stone. **Pomjane** — the unreadable village in the inscription's last line — is a place-name new to this archive.
