**The surname survey puts the name in four more Istrian places.** *Atti* 50 (2020) lists it under **GALLIGNANA** — which is **Gračišće** — and under **VISINADA/Vižinada**, **BARBAN** and **KRŠIKLA**, together with two compound forms this archive has never recorded: **Defranceschi Triscoli** and **Defranceschi Pelosi**.

**Three more, each of a different kind.** A woman holding land: *«**Elena Defranceschi** Vittorio 669 Dobasnizza Polje»* in Carlo Hugues, *Il carbonato calcico* (Parenzo 1896), a register of Istrian vineyard plots. A political line-up: *«**FACHINETTI — MADONIZZA - DEFRANCESCHI**»* in Pacifico Valussi, *Trieste e l'Istria* (Milano **1861**) — the name set beside the two best-known Istrian liberals of the year. And a citation: *«Fra i moderni citiamo **Carlo Defranceschi: «L'Istria», note storiche, Parenzo**»*, G. E. Pons, *Antichità polesi* (Pola 1910).

**And the spaced spelling opens the scholarship.** 43 records against 10. *Vjesnik Istarskog arhiva* 25 (2018) carries Jurković's bibliography of the journal's first twenty-five volumes, and it indexes **four authors of the name: DE FRANCESCHI, Camillo · Carlo · **Ettore** · **Paolo***. **Ettore and Paolo are new here.** The same volume cites *Camillo DE FRANCESCHI, Storia documentata della Contea di Pisino, a cura del figlio* — edited by his son, which names a generation.

*Method: `digitalna.nsk.hr`, «Cjeloviti tekst» box. The old `dnc.nsk.hr` portal is a dead shell and should not be cited again.*

rows.src: JUSP Jasenovac — the named victims list, on the surname and on both her married names
rows.what: Whether Anka Nera, or anyone of the name, is among the named victims of the Jasenovac camps
rows.got:
**Nobody of this name is in it, in any spelling — and Anka is not in it under either married name.**

The Jasenovac Memorial Site publishes its *Poimenični popis žrtava*, the named list of victims of the Jasenovac and Stara Gradiška camps, searchable free by surname. **Defranceschi: 0. Defranceski: 0. Franceschi: 0.**

**The control was run first**, because a nil from a search box proves nothing until the box is known to answer: *Horvat* returns pages of results, with father's name, birth year, birthplace and nationality on each row. So the zeros are evidence.

**Her married name returns four people and none of them is her.** *Oreščanin* gives **Đuro** (b. 1894, Karlovac), **Jelena** (b. 1878, Inđija), **Ljubomir** (b. 1906, Zagreb) and **Ranko** (b. 1894, Inđija) — all recorded as Serbs, none a woman born at Crikvenica in 1915. *Geiger* gives two, **Đeno-Jeno** (b. 1884, Subotica) and **Julio** (b. 1913, Zagreb), both recorded as Jews and neither her first husband — who died in **1936**, before any of this.

**What the second negative is worth.** Arolsen already said she died outside the **German** system. Jasenovac now says she died outside the **Ustaša camp** system too. A Croatian woman of twenty-nine dead in **Belgrade in 1944** is therefore not a camp death that the family softened into a city name — **she died in the city, and the records that would say how are Serbian, not Croatian and not German**.

*And the nil has a second use: it is the first time the whole surname has been put to a victims list. For a study of the name rather than of one family, «nobody of this name is in Jasenovac» is a finding in its own right.*

rows.src: Crikvenica marriages 1895 — Petar Kovačina, joiner, and the resort being built
rows.what: Reading the marriage film for Defranceschi turned up the other side of the family instead
rows.got:
**The film was being read for a name that is not in it, and gave a different one that is.**

**Crikvenica marriages 1895, entry 28, 28 November: «Petar Kovačina, stolar» — a joiner — marries «Marija Car», at Crikvenica house 119.** Both are entered as workers; his father is another **Petar Kovačina**.

**Kovačina is Uršula's surname.** **Uršula Kovačina**, born at Crikvenica about 1890–95, married **Anton Rudolf Defranceschi** and is David's great-grandmother — she is on [the direct line](/direct-line/) and died at Belgrade in 1975. A **Kovačina household at Crikvenica in 1895, in the joiner's trade, with a house number**, is the first time this archive has seen her family in a register rather than in a tree. *inf — kinship is not yet proved; a Kovačina at Crikvenica in 1895 is very likely her kin, but which kin is a question for the birth register.*

**What settles it:** the **Crikvenica births for 1890–1896**, which are on [the errands](/errands/) already for a different reason, would show whether Uršula is a daughter of this house.

**And the page it sits on is worth reading for its own sake.** The same three images carry **Josip Butković, deputy manager of the Grande Hotel**; two carpenters named **Stumpfhuber**; **Alojzije Jerkini, architect and clerk of works**; labourers from **Ljubljana**; a clerk from **Karlovac-Dubovac** with a **Herbst** witness; and a **post-and-telegraph official from Gospić** married with a **plemeniti Budisavljević** standing witness. **Crikvenica's Grand Hotel was going up, and the register is full of the people building and running it.** That is the world an Italian-named craftsman would have belonged to — and the name is still not there.

rows.src: Crikvenica marriages 1899 — a Kalanj in the book, and he is not Anna's brother
rows.what: The second surname of the Klenovica marriage finally appears in the Crikvenica register
rows.got:
**Crikvenica marriages, 1899, entry 1, 8 January: «Ivan Kalanj, zidar» — a mason — marries «Vjekoslava Car, poljodjelka».** His parents are **Ivan Kalanj and Josipa née Šilić**, labourers; hers are Jakov Car, a sailor, and Marija née Kalnić.

**Kalanj is the surname this archive has been hunting alongside Defranceschi.** **Anna Kalanj** married **Josip Defranceschi** and is Anton Rudolf's mother; the marriage this whole film was opened to find is *theirs*. So a Kalanj in the Crikvenica book matters.

**And the parents rule him out as her brother, which is worth saying plainly.** Anna Kalanj was baptised at **Ledenice in 1864**, «daughter of **Josephus Kalanj and Rosalia née Perković**, at Rijenovica house 22». This groom's parents are **Ivan and Josipa née Šilić**. **Different household.** He is not her brother, and nothing here connects him to her beyond the surname.

*What it does establish* is that **Kalanj was present at Crikvenica** and marrying there — the name is in the parish, in the building trades, in 1899. That is a place to look for Anna's kin that this archive did not have, and it sharpens the question the film was opened to answer: **the Kalanj were reachable from Crikvenica, and the Defranceschi still are not in it.**

rows.src: Crikvenica marriages 1899 — Anna Kalanj's brother, found by reading the film that does not contain her husband
rows.what: Whether any Kalanj of Anna's own household appears in the Crikvenica register
rows.got:
**Crikvenica marriages, 1899, entry 12, 25 January:**

> *«**Josip Kalanj, zidar**, iz **Ledenica**» — a mason, of **Ledenice house 37** — marries *«**Marija Poštrenčić, švelja**»*, a seamstress, now living at Crikvenica. His parents: **«Josip Kalanj i Rosalija rodj. Perković»**. A witness: **«Luka Kalanj Martinov, zidar»**.

**Those are Anna Kalanj's parents.** This archive already held her baptism: **Ledenice, 1864, «entry 2, daughter of Josephus Kalanj and Rosalia née Perković, at Rijenovica house 22»**. Same father's name, same mother, same maiden name, same parish. **Josip Kalanj the younger is Anna's brother** — and therefore **Anton Rudolf's maternal uncle** and David's great-great-uncle.

**Why it matters more than one name.** Anna Kalanj married **Josip Defranceschi**, and this whole film was opened to find *that* marriage. The film does not contain it. But it does contain **her brother**, with a **trade**, a **house number** and a **wife** — so the bride's family is now in a register rather than on a chart, and **the Kalanj turn out to be masons**, the same building trade that fills these pages while Crikvenica's hotel was going up.

**The house number differs and that is expected**: Anna is at **Rijenovica 22** in 1864, her brother at **Ledenice 37** in 1899. Rijenovica is a hamlet of Ledenice and thirty-five years separate the two entries.

**And a second Kalanj stands beside him** — *Luka Kalanj, son of Martin, mason*. A third, **Ivan Kalanj**, married in this same register three weeks earlier (1899 no. 1) to different parents. **There is a Kalanj colony of masons working between Ledenice and Crikvenica in 1899.**

*doc — the parents' names are read directly off the page; the maiden name «Perković» is a handwriting read, checked at full magnification.*

**What to do next:** the **Ledenice marriage register** should hold Josip and Marija's banns, and the **Ledenice births around 1860–1875** should hold Anna and her brothers together in one household — which would give this archive **Anna's whole sibling set** for the first time.

rows.src: Novi Vinodolski — the parish that serves Klenovica, checked at the source
rows.what: Whether the marriage of Josip Defranceschi and Anna Kalanj can be found at Novi Vinodolski, the parish named as the next place to look when the Crikvenica film came up empty
rows.got:
**It cannot, and the reason is worth writing down rather than repeating the guess.**

**Novi Vinodolski has no marriage register on film after 1859.** Queried directly against the FamilySearch waypoint tree rather than against this archive's own harvested copy: the parish has **seven** filmed volumes, and its only marriage books are **Vjenčani 1674–1786** and **Vjenčani 1787–1859**. The rest are baptisms (1650–1784, 1784–1804, 1804–1852, 1852–1874, **1875–1900**) and deaths (1784–1823, 1823–1859, 1859–1888, 1888–1899). *There is no volume in which this marriage could be.*

**And Anton Rudolf is not in Novi's baptism book either — which is the part that actually teaches something.** He was born at **Klenovica house 22 on 20 January 1890, baptised 9 February**, and Klenovica sits in the Novi Vinodolski municipality, so the 1875–1900 baptism volume was the obvious place. It was opened and the entries around that date were read: **image 249 closes 1889 and opens 1890 at entries 1–4** (1, 4, 12 and 4 January); **image 250 runs entries 5–11**, 14 January to 6 April; **image 251 runs 12–19**, to late June. **No Defranceschi anywhere in them.**

**Because Klenovica had its own church.** This archive's own plate of the baptism says so in the priest's words — *«u ovoj župnoj crkvi»*, in **this** parish church — and the register it comes from is catalogued not under Novi but as **«Matične knjige, Ledenice / Klenovica»**. **Klenovica does not exist as a parish in the FamilySearch tree at all**, so its books are not filmed and cannot be read this way.

**One line of that entry redirects the whole search.** The remarks column explains why the birth happened at Klenovica at all: *«Roditelji djeteta nahodeć se kod svojih u Klenovici, t.j. kod roditelja žene Ane, dobiše ovo djete»* — **the parents, being with their own people at Klenovica, that is with the parents of the wife Ana, had this child.** So in January 1890 the couple **did not live at Klenovica**. They were visiting. **Klenovica is Ana's parents' house, not theirs** — which is consistent with the godfather being **Jakov Kalanj of that same house 22**.

*nil — the register that would answer the question is not on film; the register that was on film has been read and does not contain them.*

rows.src: Sv. Jakov-Šiljevica marriages 1882–1891 — read end to end
rows.what: Whether Josip Defranceschi and Anna Kalanj married in the small Vinodol parish next to Klenovica, whose marriage film — contrary to this archive's earlier survey — does cover the years wanted
rows.got:
**Ten years read, both surnames visible on every line, and the name is not there.**

The volume is **Vjenčani 1859–1910**, eighty-three images for fifty-one years — a parish of six to ten marriages a year. Its left page carries **both spouses with their condition, the origin and domicile of each, religion, age and status**, so a single crop of the left page shows every surname and every place in the entry.

**Images 35 to 46 were read: 1882 from entry 5, then 1883, 1884, 1885, 1886, 1887, 1888, 1889, 1890 and 1891 complete.** That covers the whole window in which this marriage can fall — Ana Kalanj was born in January 1864 and her first known child in January 1890.

**Year totals, off the priest's own numbering:** 1882 closes at 10, 1883 at 5, 1884 at 8, 1885 at 6, 1886 at 10, 1887 at 7, 1888 at 7, 1889 at 4, 1890 at 6 or more, 1891 at 5 or more. **About seventy marriages, and not one Defranceschi.**

**It is a closed parish of eight surnames.** *Grbić/Grbčić, Abel, Crhak, Šegulja, Turčić, Pavlić, Damian, Šepac, Malčić, Perhat, Knez, Blažić, Mlanfar* — marrying each other between **Klošter, Šiljevica, Smokovo, Katun, Sv. Jakov** and **Mlanfari**. **Klenovica never appears in the origin column at all**, which is itself an answer: this parish did not serve it.

**Two outsiders in ten years, and the register named both in full** — **Mate Piškulić, kr. financijski čuvar**, a royal finance guard of Novi marrying a Trsat woman domiciled at Kraljevica (1882 no. 10), and **a miller with an Italian surname from «Piran — Istrija»** marrying a Turčić (1890 no. 6). *The same test as at Crikvenica: when a stranger married here the clerk wrote down his trade and his birthplace. Ours never had to be written.*

*nil — ten complete years, left page of every spread, both surname columns.*

rows.src: A catalogue correction: two Vinodol parishes DO have marriage films covering 1883–1889
rows.dest: Vinodol — Bribir, Sv. Jakov-Šiljevica, Ledenice, Novi Vinodolski
rows.what: Re-checking the shelf survey that sent this archive to Crikvenica, against the live FamilySearch waypoint tree rather than a harvested copy
rows.got:
**The survey that opened the Crikvenica film said that across the whole Vinodol only one marriage register on film reached the 1880s. That was wrong by two parishes.**

Queried parish by parish on 20 September 2026:

| parish | marriage volumes on film | covers 1883–89? |
|---|---|---|
| **Crikvenica** | 1800–1858 · **1859–1908** | yes — **read, negative** |
| **Bribir** | 1678–1738 · 1815–1821, 1853–1858 · **1858–1900** | **yes — not yet read** |
| **Sv. Jakov-Šiljevica** | 1821–1859 · **1859–1910** | **yes — read, negative** |
| Ledenice | 1734–1825 · 1826–1865 · 1866–**1882** | no |
| Novi Vinodolski | 1674–1786 · 1787–**1859** | no |
| Grižane | 1735–1858 only | no |

**So the field was never as narrow as the earlier note claimed.** Sv. Jakov-Šiljevica has now been read and is clean. **Bribir, Vjenčani 1858–1900, remains unread and is the last filmed Vinodol marriage register that could hold this marriage.**

*correction — recorded against this archive's own earlier statement, not against anybody else's.*

rows.src: Bribir marriages 1882–1890 — the last filmed Vinodol marriage register, read end to end
rows.what: The final filmed candidate for the marriage of Josip Defranceschi and Anna Kalanj — nine consecutive years covering the whole window in which it must fall
rows.got:
**Nine years, close to four hundred marriages, both surnames legible on every line, and the name is not there.**

**First, a trap in the catalogue worth recording.** The waypoint for *Vjenčani 1858–1900* returns **597 images**, because Bribir's births, marriages and deaths share one reel and the catalogue gives them the same film ark. Probing found deaths at images 300, 420, 480 and 540 and **the marriages around image 120**. The marriage section runs roughly **images 108–150**; everything from about 250 onward is the death register.

**Year by year, off the priest's own numbering:**

| year | marriages | pages |
|---|---|---|
| 1883 | **57** | 102–106 |
| 1884 | **45** | 107–109 |
| 1885 | **64** | 110–113 |
| 1886 | **41** | 114–116 |
| 1887 | **45** | 117–120 |
| 1888 | **25** | 121–125 |
| 1889 | **22** | 126–129 |
| 1890 | **24** | 130–132 |

With the tail of 1882 that is **about four hundred marriages read**, and **no Defranceschi in any of them.**

**Bribir is the biggest of these parishes and the most closed.** Sixty-four marriages in 1885, most of them crammed into the three weeks before Lent — twelve on 11 January alone. And they are the same thirty surnames over and over: **Antonić, Krsul, Krajačić, Kalafatić, Dražić, Simac, Špoja, Tonković, Skvirić, Juden, Kombol, Stanić, Čor, Ugrin, Pipinić, Škočilić, Marinčić, Pohmajević** — marrying each other between **Štale, Podgori, Kričina, Sv. Vid, Sv. Mikula, Kosavin, Jargovo, Dragaljin, Gradac, Podskoči, Ugrin** and **Podugrinac**.

**The outsiders are countable and the register named every one.** *Paskval Freca «iz Rieke, u Bribiru nastanjen»* and *Fran Bontić of Rijeka* (1883); *Lovre Krmpotić of **Ledenice*** (1885); a bride from **Novi** (1886); *Mate Barac of **Grižane*** (1888); **Luka Roman Josip Vrinjanin, merchant, of Krasica donja, domiciled at Crikvenica** (1889); *Stanko Belošević, joiner, of Petrovsko near Krapina* (1889). And the best of them, **1888 no. 22: «G. Ulrich Hofer, mjestni učitelj pučke učione» of Karlovac marrying «Teresia Antolić, učiteljica ovdašnje pučke učione» of Zagreb** — the village schoolmaster and schoolmistress marrying each other, both written down with their posts.

**Method note, because the film fought back.** The reel photographs the whole spread in one frame with wide black margins, so the Crikvenica crop did not fit; the working left-page window is `x 0.085 w 0.300, y 0.055 h 0.855`. An early crop at `h 0.64` clipped the last two or three entries of each page — **the gaps that created (p.104 nos 35–36 and p.105 no. 48) were gone back for and filled**, so the run is continuous. The reel also carries **duplicate frames** (images 114 and 115 are the same page), so pages, not images, are the unit that matters.

*nil — 1882 in part, then 1883 to 1890 complete, left page of every spread, no gaps.*

rows.src: Anna Kalanj's whole household, and the house she was born in
rows.what: The sibling set of Anna Kalanj, and whether the Kalanj house at Klenovica can be tied to the house in her own baptism
rows.got:
**Eight children, and the same front door for thirty years.**

The **Ledenice baptism register 1861–1894** gives the children of **Josip Kalanj and Rosalija née Perković** — David's great-great-grandparents on the Kvarner side. Found through the FamilySearch index on `q.fatherSurname=Kalanj`, then **every one of them read back on the register page itself**:

| child | born | baptised | house as the clerk wrote it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Thomas** | 1858 | — | *(earlier volume, not yet read on the page)* |
| **Martinus** | 10 Nov 1861 | — | **«Ledenice in Klenovica N° 22»** |
| **ANNA** | **3 Jan 1864** | **6 Jan** | **«Rljinovica N° 22»** |
| **Lucia** | 24 May 1866 | — | **«Ledenice N° 22, in Rljenovice»** |
| **Franciscus** | 30 Sep 1868 | — | *(parents verified; locus not yet read)* |
| **Josephus** | **5 May 1871** | **7 May** | **«Povile N° 22»** |
| **Maria** | 19 Mar 1874 | — | *(parents verified; locus not yet read)* |
| **Joannes** | 18/20 Jul 1877 | — | **«Povile N° 2…»** |

**Anna's own entry, page 24, entry 2, read at full magnification:** born **3 January 1864**, baptised **6 January**, *legitima*, of **«Josephus Kalanj … et Rosalia nata Perković ejus uxor, ruricolae»**, at **Rljinovica N° 22**, godparents **Josephus Ban and his wife Anna**, baptised by **Vincentius Šegulja, parochus administrator**. *This also reconciles two dates that looked like a contradiction: the archive had 3 January, the index says 6 January. They are the birth and the baptism, and both are right.*

## The house

**The clerk names one house four ways across sixteen years — Klenovica, Rljinovica, Rljenovice, Povile — and the number never changes. It is always 22.** In 1861 he writes it out in full: **«Ledenice in Klenovica N° 22»**.

**And Anton Rudolf Defranceschi was born at «Klenovica kbr. 22» on 20 January 1890.**

So **Anna Kalanj was born in the same house as her son**, twenty-six years apart, and the 1890 baptism's remark — *«kod roditelja žene Ane»*, with the wife Ana's parents — is naming **this** household. The godfather of 1890, **Jakov Kalanj of house 22**, belongs to it too.

*One honest caveat.* Klenovica, Rijenovica and Povile are three named places on and above that stretch of coast. The 1861 entry ties **Klenovica** and **22** to these exact parents, and 1864 and 1866 tie **Rijenovica** and **22** to them; **Povile 22** in 1871 and 1877 may be the same house under a neighbouring hamlet's name or a short move along the shore. **The number, the parish and the parents are firm; which of the three names the building itself stood under is not settled by these entries alone.**

## What it gives the archive

**Anna Kalanj stops being a name on a chart.** She is the **third of eight**, with an elder brother Thomas and Martinus above her and five below — and the youngest of them, **Josephus, born 5 May 1871**, is exactly the **«Josip Kalanj, zidar, of Ledenice house 37»** who married Marija Poštrenčić at Crikvenica in January 1899 and was identified as her brother from that entry's parents. **The two findings now confirm each other from opposite ends.**

*doc — index used only to locate the pages; every date and every house number above that is not marked otherwise was read off the register image.*

rows.src: The index, asked straight out for a Defranceschi married to a Kalanj
rows.what: Whether the marriage of Josip Defranceschi and Anna Kalanj is anywhere in the FamilySearch index, in any parish in Croatia
rows.got:
**It is not, and the question had never been put this way.**

Two queries against the Croatia Church Books index, on the fields that actually work: **`q.spouseSurname=Kalanj`** across Croatia, and **`q.surname=Defranceschi / Defranceski / Franceschi`** across Croatia. Six hundred rows came back for the surname and a hundred for the Kalanj spouse.

**Every «Franc-» name among the Kalanj marriages is a forename or a different surname** — *Franciscus, Francisca, Franković, Frković*. **There is no marriage of a Defranceschi to a Kalanj in the index at all.**

*That is the expected answer and it is worth having explicitly.* The index only knows what has been filmed, and the register this marriage should be in — **Klenovica, or Ledenice after 1882** — is not filmed. **A negative from the index is not a negative from the record.**

rows.src: The surname put straight to the index — and two children's entries read back
rows.what: What the FamilySearch index holds for the name in the Vinodol, checked row by row against the register images
rows.got:
**Six hundred indexed rows for the name in Croatia; fifteen touch the Vinodol; two of them matter, and they pull in opposite directions.**

**1. A correction. «Marija Stjepanka Defranceschi, 22 Dec 1892, Ledenice».** This archive had her as *born 8 December 1892 at Crikvenica*. The page — **Ledenice baptisms p.166 no. 83** — says born **8 December**, baptised **22 December**, at **Ledenice**, of **«Josip Defranceschi, klesar, i žena Ana Kalanj rodjena»**, residence **«Klenovica kbroj 28, na stan»** — Klenovica house 28, **in lodgings**. *So the family were still in the Ledenice parish at the end of 1892, living in rented rooms a few doors from Ana's parents at house 22.* Logged as [a correction](/corrections/).

**2. A confirmation, and the index is the one that is wrong.** The index gives *«Zorica De Franceski, Jul 1897, Crikvenica»*; this archive has her born **14 December 1896**. The page — **Crikvenica baptisms p.299 no. 143** — says born **14 December 1896**, baptised **17 January 1897**. **The archive's date is right and the index garbled it.** The entry is worth having for its own sake: the father is written **«Josip Defranceschi Antonov iz Gračišća, klesar u mjestu»** — *son of Anton, of Gračišće, stonecutter in this place*. **The Istrian origin and the patronymic are written into a Kvarner register in the priest's own hand.**

*The lesson is the one this archive keeps relearning: the index is a finding aid and nothing more. Both rows had to be read on the page, and one of them was wrong.*

rows.src: The Kovačina marriage of 1895 — and the question the archive refused to guess at
rows.what: Whether Petar Kovačina the joiner of house 119 was the financial guard under an earlier trade, a brother, or a son
rows.got:
**He is the son, and the marriage entry says so in as many words.**

This archive set the question out honestly and declined to answer it: two Crikvenica death entries gave a **Petar Kovačina, «umirovljeni c. kr. financijski Nadstražar»**, who died on 3 November 1904 aged 55 with his wife **Uršula née Stojčić**, and a **Petar Kovačina, «stolar»**, a joiner, married to **Marija née Car** — *both at house 119*. *«Whether the joiner is the guard under an earlier trade, a brother, or a son, the register does not say and this archive will not guess.»*

**The marriage register does say.** Crikvenica marriages, **28 November 1895**, entry 28 — read on the film, and the parents' cell magnified to be certain of it:

> **«Petar Kovačina, stolar»** marries **«Marija Car»** at **Crikvenica house 119**.
> **Parents of the groom: «Petar Kovačina, k. r. financ. nadstražar, i Uršula rodj. Stojčić, radnica.»**
> Parents of the bride: **«Vjekoslav Car i [Krista?] rodj. Car»** — *the mother’s forename reads as **Krista** on the page and is indexed as **Vinka**; the surname and the father are not in doubt, the forename is.*

**Those are exactly the two people from the 1904 death entry** — the same name, the same office in the same words, the same wife with the same maiden name. **The joiner is the guard's son.**

**So the house resolves into three generations:**

1. **Petar Kovačina the elder** — *c. kr. financijski nadstražar*, a senior guard of the Habsburg customs and excise, born at **Draga in the kotar of Sušak** about 1849, dead of consumption at Crikvenica on **3 November 1904**; and **Uršula «Ursa» née Stojčić**, *kućarka*.
2. **Petar Kovačina the younger** — **stolar**, a joiner — who married **Marija Car** on **28 November 1895** and kept house 119. The observations add why the wedding needed paperwork: *«dozvolom kr. ug. Ministarstva za zem. obranu od 14/9 t.g. br. 53688»* — **by leave of the Royal Hungarian Ministry of National Defence**, so he was still of service age. Their daughter **Josipa** died there at eighteen months in September 1898.
3. **Uršula Kovačina**, who married **Anton Rudolf Defranceschi** — *and who carries her grandmother's name*.

**One step is inference and is flagged as such.** That Anton Rudolf's wife Uršula is the daughter of the joiner and Marija Car is the natural reading — the name, the house and the dates all fit a girl born at 119 in the later 1890s — **but it is not yet proved**. The proof would be her own baptism: **Crikvenica births, 1896–1902, a Uršula Kovačina at house 119.** That is the next thing to read.

*doc for the three named generations; the link from the joiner to Anton Rudolf's wife is inf until that baptism is found.*

**And the next step was tried at once: it does not answer.** The index was queried for every child of a Kovačina father in Croatia — four hundred rows — and **there is no Uršula Kovačina birth in it at all**. Either her baptism is unindexed or she was born outside these books. *So the link from the joiner to Anton Rudolf’s wife stays exactly where it was: the natural reading, not yet the proved one.* Reading Crikvenica births 1896–1902 page by page is the way to settle it.

rows.src: The FamilySearch index, matched on Valentino and Helena as parents rather than on the children's names

rows.what: An ark and an image for each of Valentino's Fiume children, so the pages stop resting on an unciteable reading

**Eleven of fifteen recovered, a fifteenth child found, and the four that resist are exactly the four the archive had already named as unindexed.**

Searching the index for the children's names fails, because the names are latinised differently in every entry. **Searching the surname and then filtering on date works**: `q.surname` over *Defranceschi*, *De Franceschi* and *Franceschi*, keeping only rows whose principal carries a year between **1735 and 1760**. Twenty-two rows come back for those twenty-five years; eleven of them are Valentino's.
