rows.src: Fiume baptisms, the page under «Die 21 July 1757»
rows.what: Whether the index's «Jacobum Vincentium» of Valentinus and Helena is really a child of this household
rows.got:
**He is, and the entry is unambiguous.**

The first crop of the frame landed on the **20 July** heading and showed *«Margaritam Annam … jugalium Danesich»* — not a Defranceschi — which briefly looked like the index pointing at the wrong page. It was not: the index gives **born 20 July, baptised 21 July**, and the entry sits under the *next* date heading, below the crop. Reading further down the same page:

> **«Die 21 July 1757 — Jacobum Vincentium filium legitimum Valentini, et Helenæ jugalium Defranceschi, natum 20 hujus, baptizavit D. Carolus Simon Bertoni, Patrini fuere Ill.mus D. Emanuel de Perretti, et Ill.ma D.na Elisabeth Bono.»**

**Two things beyond the name.** The godparents are styled ***Illustrissimus*** and ***Illustrissima*** — de Perretti and Bono are Fiume patrician names, and a Carnian immigrant's son does not get those sponsors by accident eighteen years after being made a citizen. And the child is **the tenth son**, which is the number the family has always given and the number this archive could not reach while it had fourteen children.

*doc — [image](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99F-WWGH).*

rows.src: Fiume burials, September 1757, entry 14
rows.what: Whether Aloysia was really «born and buried 1757», since that cannot stand beside a brother born in July of the same year
rows.got:
**She was four years old, so she was born about 1753 and the conflict disappears.**

The frame is an Italian burial book, numbered, each entry *«d’anni X, figlia di …, sepolta con Bara nella …»*, under a **Settembre 1757** heading. Entry 14:

> **«Alovisia d’anni 4, figlia di Valentino, ed Elena Defranceschi, sepolta nella Tomba di …»**

**The unit is deliberate.** Entries on the same page that record infants give months — *«Maria di mesi 3»* two lines above — so «d’anni 4» means four years, not four months. The digit was magnified to be sure of it, and matches the «d’anni 4» of the entry immediately below.

**What it changes.** The archive had her as one of five infants «born and buried 1757». She was instead a child of about four, **born c. 1753**, and the 1757 date is her burial alone. *doc — [image](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99F-QD3H).*

rows.src: Maria's 1757 burial — the question Aloysia's entry raised
rows.what: Whether Maria, like her sister Aloysia, was older than an infant when she was buried in 1757
rows.got:
**She was an infant — the register says months, not years — so Aloysia's case does not repeat. But the count is off by a few months at the other end.**

The frame is the same Italian burial book, under a **Maggio 1757** heading. Entry 20:

> **«20. Maria figlia di Valentio, ed Elena Defranceschi **di mesi …**, sepolta con S.B. nella Tomba di S. Giovanni.»**

**The unit is the whole answer.** Aloysia's entry, four months later in the same book, reads *«d’anni 4»*; Maria's reads *«di mesi»*. The clerk distinguishes the two, and the line above Maria's — another Maria, of Giovanni and Maria Babi — splits the difference with *«d’un anno e mè»*. So Maria Defranceschi died in her first year.

**The numeral itself will not resolve.** Magnified twice, it sits against the gutter shadow at the line's end and reads as one or two minims — **1, 6 and 11 are all possible and this archive will not choose between them.** That matters a little: buried in **May 1757**, an infant of eleven months was **born in 1756**, one of a month or six in **1757**. Her entry accordingly no longer claims a birth year.

*doc for the burial and for «di mesi»; the age in months and the birth year are unread.*

rows.src: Fiume, St Vitus baptisms, film 005497925 — read at four dates no index reaches
rows.what: The four children of Valentino Defranceschi whose baptisms appear in no index anywhere, and whose pages therefore rested on a reading nobody could check
rows.got:
**All four found, all four exactly where the 6 September reading said, and three of them gave up a birth date that reading had not recorded.**

**How the frames were found, since this is reusable.** Any image ark resolves to a film and a frame number: `/service/records/storage/dascloud/das/v2/3:1:<ARK>` returns `{"name":"005497925_00293"}` — film 005497925, frame 293. Feeding the eleven indexed children through that gives eleven dated frames, and the gaps between them can be interpolated to about a frame either way. The film's own `/children` endpoint is refused by their security service and **was not pushed at**; the ordinary browse route — `/search/film/005497925?i=<n>`, whose page title carries the `wc=` waypoint — gives the same list legitimately. The film holds several volumes: frames 1–205 under waypoint `9R2X-ZNT:…714201`, frames 206 onward under `9R2X-C62:…714501`. **Do not interpolate across the join** — the two volumes run at different rates, about 9 frames a year before it and about 12 after.

| child | frame | the entry |
|---|---|---|
| **Ignatius Francus Mattheus** | 126 | «Die 29 Julij 1745 — Ignatium Franc.um Matthæum filium legitimum **D.ni Valentini, et Helenæ jugalium De Franceschi**, **heri natum**» |
| **Vitus Joannes Baptista** | 228 | «Die 18 Junij 1751 — Vitum Joannem Baptistam filium legitimum **D.ni Valentini, et D.næ Helenæ jugalium Defranceschi**, baptizavit D. Petrus Eustachius … Decanus» |
| **Aloysius Rochus** | 257 | «Die 18 Augusti 1754 — Aloysium Rochum filium legitimum **D.ni Valentini, et Helenæ jugalium Defranceschi, natum 16 hujus**» |
| **Rosalia Francisca** | 272 | «Die 8 8bris 1755 — Rosaliam Franciscam filiam legitimam **D.ni Valentini et Helenæ jugalium Defranceschi, natam 3a hujus**» |

**Three new birth dates**, from the registers' habit of saying how long ago the child was born: Ignatius **28 July 1745** (*heri natum*, born yesterday), Aloysius Rochus **16 August 1754**, Rosalia Francisca **3 October 1755**.

**And something the index could never have shown.** By the 1750s the clerk writes **D.nus Valentinus** and **D.na Helena** — *Dominus*, not plain Valentino — and the godparents are styled ***Illustrissimus*** and ***Illustrissima***: in 1754 «Ill.mus D.nus Joannes Josephus Carolus Borghesi, et Ill.ma Domicella **Lib. Bar. de Benzoni**» — a **free baroness** — and in 1757 «Ill.mus D. Emanuel de Perretti, et Ill.ma D.na Elisabeth Bono». **The Carnian who was made a citizen in 1739 was having his children held at the font by the patriciate of Fiume fifteen years later.** That is a social fact, and it is only on the page.

*doc — every one of the fifteen children now cites the image it stands on. Item 126 is closed.*

rows.src: Crikvenica births 1896, read entry by entry — and the reason 1897 cannot be read at all
rows.what: Uršula Kovačina, daughter of Petar Kovačina the joiner and Marija Car of house 119 — the baptism that would prove Anton Rudolf's wife is the guard's granddaughter
rows.got:
**She is not there, and the years she is most likely to be in are not filmed. This closes the FamilySearch route and hands the question to Rijeka.**

**What was read.** Crikvenica **Births (Rođeni) 1859–1896**, waypoint `9R28-RMH:…391676801`, **images 673 to 697** — the whole of 1896, about a hundred and fifty births, six to a spread. Every parents' surname and every house number was read. The surnames are Car, Katnić, Matejčić, Župan, Lovrić, Brozičević, Grbičić, Škiljan, Veljacić, Jurinčić, over and over. **There is no Kovačina birth in Crikvenica in 1896 at all.**

**Two Uršulas turned up and neither is ours** — «Urša Marija» of Martin Car at house 102, and «Urša» of Gergo Zanković at house 125. The name was common in the parish, which is worth knowing before anyone reads a later book hopefully.

**And now the wall.** The parish's filmed birth volumes are **1815–1823, 1855–1858, 1822–1855** and **1859–1896**, and that is all. **Crikvenica births from 1897 onward are not on film.** Uršula's parents married on **28 November 1895**, so a first child before the autumn of 1896 is barely possible and none was registered; her sister **Josipa died at eighteen months in September 1898**, which puts Josipa's birth at about March 1897. **The whole plausible window for Uršula falls in the unfilmed years.**

**So the link stays inference, and the way to settle it is now named.** Neither the index (four hundred Kovačina rows, no Uršula) nor the film can reach her. The Crikvenica register for 1897–1902 is with the **Državni arhiv u Rijeci**, which is exactly what work-list **141**'s letter asks for. *nil — and the negative is worth as much as a hit, because it stops anyone reading 1896 again.*

rows.src: Zorica's own baptism entry, at the foot of the last filmed page
rows.what: An image and a citation for Zorica, born 14 December 1896 — found while reading the year for somebody else
rows.got:
**She is the last birth entered in the book, and the entry changes something the archive believed about the name.**

Reading 1896 for a Kovačina that is not there turned up a Defranceschi that is. The final entry on **image 696** is **Zorica**, *zakonita*, and her father is written **«Josip Defran=ceski Antonov»** — *klesar*, a stonecutter — with the household placed as **«Iz Istrije mjesto Gračišće, sad ovdje stanujući»**: from Istria, the place Gračišće, now dwelling here.

**Three things come out of it.**

**The spelling.** The surname is written **Defranceski** — magnified twice, the second line is c-e-s-k-i, no *ch*. This archive had dated that form to the twentieth century and the diaspora. **A Croatian priest wrote it in the home parish in 1896**, before anyone left. See the correction.

**The address.** There is **no house number**. Where every other family on the page has one, this one is entered by its origin — the register's way of marking incomers. Six years after Anton Rudolf was born at Klenovica 22, the family were still being written down as people from somewhere else.

**The trade, again.** *Klesar* — the same word used of Josip at Marija Stjepanka's baptism at Ledenice in 1892 and at Ivan's death in 1896, and the trade his father Antonius held at Gračišće in 1863. Three parishes, three clerks, one word.

*doc — [image](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-R9WZ-V), Crikvenica births 1859–1896, film image 696.*

rows.src: Johann Defranceschi of Gallignana, born 1833 — tried in the index and tried on the shelf
rows.what: The Gračišće baptism of 1833 that would give parents to the sailor in the three Kriegsarchiv files
rows.got:
**Neither route exists, and one of them this archive had told itself did.**

**The index first.** Every *Defranceschi* and *De Franceschi* birth in the Croatia collection with a year between **1825 and 1842** was pulled — forty-five rows. They sit at Kaštelir, Tar, Pola, Fiume, Tarsatica and a scatter of «Croazia, Austria». **There is no Gračišće entry among them, and no Johann or Giovanni born 1833 anywhere in the set.**

**Then the film — and here the archive was wrong about itself.** Work-list 135 said *«the Gračišće baptisms of 1833 are on film and readable from here»*. **They are not.** Gračišće is not a parish in the FamilySearch Croatia collection at all: a search of all thousand parish nodes returns only **Pazin**, **Stari Pazin** and **Lupoglav (Pazin)** for that corner of Istria, and none of their volume lists contains a Gračišće book. This archive's **own atlas already said so** — the Gračišće place record carries **`nfilms: 0`** — so the work-list note contradicted the map for days.

**Gračišće is one of the unfilmed parishes**, which is exactly the class this archive counted in September: *495 of the 1,151 books in the Pazin inventory are in parishes with no film at all*. Its registers are at **DAPA Pazin** and on the parish shelf, which is where everything this site holds from Gračišće — the 1863 baptism, the Status Animarum — already came from.

**So the route is the one that has already worked once.** DAPA Pazin refuses open-ended research but will search **a named register for a named person over a stated period** — they did exactly that on the Gračišće birth register, certified the copy and posted it to Queensland for 117 kuna. *«Johann/Giovanni Defranceschi, Gračišće, 1833»* is precisely that shape of request. *nil on both searchable routes — and the correction is worth more than the search was.*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat — which volumes are filmed, and where this archive's own reading had stopped
rows.what: Whether the castle parish can be read past 1707, where the September sweep of DGS 005497884 ended
rows.got:
**All ten volumes are on film, and the archive's own reading of them stops at 1707. Everything after that is open ground.**

Svetvinčenat sits in the collection at `9R2H-DPJ:391644801,392404501` with **ten volumes**:

| | |
|---|---|
| Births | **1568–1588** · 1589–1646 · 1663–1708, 1696–1698 · **1709–1764** · **1764–1791, 1815–1874** |
| Marriages | 1581–1589, 1622–1623 · **1762–1858, 1855–1895** |
| Deaths | 1791–1887 · 1887–1917 |

**Where this archive already is.** The nineteen openings of **DGS 005497884** read band by band in September cover **1666–1707**, plus the 1628 entry that moved the Istrian sequence. The **1709–1764** and **1764–1791** books are the next two on the shelf and had not been touched — which is why Antonio of 1780, from *Atti* 48, was still only a footnote.

**Two limits worth recording.** The **1568–1588 volume is damaged**: the film's own card reads *«TORN PAGE(S) / POTRGANA STRANICA»* and the leaf photographed is a torn wedge missing about a third of its text. And the **DAPA inventory marks all five of the old birth books «digitised: no»** (nos 4841–4845) while FamilySearch has filmed them — a reminder that the inventory's digitised column and the film are two different questions.

*yield — the shelf mapped and the gap in this archive's own reading located.*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat baptisms 1780 — the first pages of the 1764–1791 book read here
rows.what: Whether the surname the *Atti* article calls the castle's only continuous one is actually in the parish register, and whether Antonio of 1780 is a real man on a page
rows.got:
**Both households are there, a fortnight apart, in the exact year the article names — and one of them is Antonio's.**

Svetvinčenat is **unindexed**: a search of the FamilySearch persona index for every spelling of the name, filtered to this parish, returns **zero rows**. The book has to be read — which is how this archive read 1666–1707 off DGS 005497884 in September. **This is the next book on that shelf**, and it had not been opened. **Births 1764–1791**, image 81 (`3:1:3QS7-899X-K3LW`), one frame, both pages:

> **«Anno D.ni 1780. Die 16 Aprilis S. Vincentij»** — Maria, daughter of Matthæus Pieder and Maria his wife; *«Patrini ad Sacrum Fontem fuere **Dominicus Defranceschi**, et **Fosca** Uxor ejus»*.

> **«Anno D.ni 1780 Die 1 Maij S. Vincentij»** — Joannes, son of Gregorius Mathes; among the godparents *«**Mathea uxor Antonij Defranceschi**»*.

**Two distinct households**, then: **Dominicus × Fosca** and **Antonius × Mathea**, both standing at the font in the castle parish within sixteen days of each other in 1780.

**And the second name is the one that matters.** *Atti* 48 has *«Guidati da **Antonio Defranceschi**, nel **1780** avevano ottenuto l'esonero dal partecipare alla difesa armata»* — led by Antonio Defranceschi, in 1780 the castle's families got themselves excused armed defence duty. **The register has an Antonius Defranceschi at S. Vincenti in 1780**, with a wife and a place in the parish's godparent circuit. The article's leader stops being a footnote in an Italian journal and becomes a man in a book.

**What this is not.** Neither entry is a **Defranceschi baptism** — both are appearances as godparents, which is how a household first shows itself in a register but is not the same as its own children. And **nothing here ties these two to the Gologorica–Gračišće line**; these are two more households of a surname this parish already holds in quantity — the archive has **seventy-five people at Svetvinčenat** and *«at least twelve distinct fathers of this surname in one small town between 1657 and 1737»*. What is new is that they are **after 1707**, where the earlier sweep stopped. *doc for both entries; the descent is not claimed.*

*(A misreading caught on the way: Antonius's wife was first read as «Fabria» from the full-page view. Magnified, the hand is plainly **Mathea**.)*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat births 1709–1764 — the volume's own index, and then the page it points to
rows.what: A Defranceschi household in the castle parish before 1780 — their own children, not godparent appearances
rows.got:
**Found: Cattarina, daughter of Sig.r Batta de Franceschi and Anzoletta, born 10 February 1728. That is fifty-two years before Antonio's exemption, and it is the family's own child.**

**The shortcut is the finding behind the finding.** Reading 216 register frames for one surname is not sensible; the volume carries **its own contemporary index** at the back, images ~197–214. It is arranged **by the child's forename**, not by surname, each line reading *«‹Given› di ‹father's forename› ‹SURNAME› ‹date› — c. ‹carta›»*. Sixteen images replace two hundred. On those frames an index leaf faces a register leaf, so **both pages of each frame have to be read**.

On the **C** page, second line:

> **«Cattarina fig.a di D.o Batta Defranceschi 11 Feb.ro 1728 — c. 66»**

**And carta 66 is on image 77, right page**, under the heading *«Adi 5 Febbro 1728»*:

> **«Catta[rina] fig.a leg.ma di S.r Batta de Fran.chi et di Anzoletta sua Consorte, nata li 10 d.to, fu battegata da me Arcip.te Quelis; Padrini furono al S. Fonte il S.r Bortolo Francal Giudice et la S.ra Madalena moglie del Sig. Vic.o Quelis.»**

**What the entry carries beyond the names.** The father is **«S.r» — Signore**, and so is the mother's style; the godfather is **Bortolo Francal, the Giudice**, the village's own magistrate, and the godmother is the **Vicar's wife**. A household that stands at the font with the judge and the vicar's wife is not a cottager's. That is the same social register as the 1754 Fiume baptism where a **free baroness** held Valentino's son — and the two families are not known to be connected.

**On the spelling.** The register abbreviates the surname **«de Fran.chi»**; the index writes it out as **«Defranceschi»**. Both forms are the same clerk's parish, twenty years apart, and the index is the one that spells it.

**The mother's name was read twice.** «Anzoletta» — the Venetian diminutive of Angela — only resolved when the line's right-hand end was magnified against the gutter; a first pass had it as «…ica».

*doc — [image](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-KQK2), Svetvinčenat births 1709–1764, film image 77, carta 66; index entry at image 199.*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat, the D page of the index — and the same man again thirty-two years later
rows.what: A second Defranceschi household in the castle, and whether any of these people can be followed across a lifetime
rows.got:
**A second father, a second child — and that child turns up again as a grown man standing godfather in 1764.**

The index's **D** page (image 200, right), eighth line:

> **«Dom.co Gasparo di Giacomo Defranceschi 9 Ag.to 1732 — c. 80»**

So beside **Batta** and Anzoletta, whose Cattarina was born in 1728, the castle holds **Giacomo Defranceschi**, whose son **Domenico Gasparo** was baptised on **9 August 1732**.

**And the register leaf facing that very index page closes the circle.** The same frame carries baptisms of **February 1764**, and in the entry of 9 February the godfather is

> **«D. Gasparo de Franceschi figlio di Giacomo»**

— *Gasparo de Franceschi, son of Giacomo*. **That is the child of 1732, aged thirty-one, standing at the font himself.** Two independent entries in one volume, thirty-two years apart, give the same man twice: once as an infant with his father named, once as an adult with the same father named.

**What the castle now holds, on the page:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Batta de Franceschi × Anzoletta** | daughter **Cattarina**, born 10 Feb 1728, carta 66 |
| **Giacomo Defranceschi** | son **Domenico Gasparo**, 9 Aug 1732, carta 80 |
| **Gasparo de Franceschi, son of Giacomo** | godfather, 9 Feb 1764 |
| **Dominicus Defranceschi × Fosca** | godparents, 16 Apr 1780 |
| **Antonius Defranceschi × Mathea** | godmother, 1 May 1780 |

**Fifty-two years of the name in one parish, from two fathers, without leaving a single volume.** Whether Dominicus of 1780 is the Domenico Gasparo of 1732 is the obvious question and **this archive will not answer it from a forename**; the 1764 entry shows the man was called *Gasparo*, not *Domenico*, by the people who knew him.

*doc — [image](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-KQS3) for the index line and the 1764 entry, both on film image 200; carta 80 itself not yet opened.*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat index, letters C to G read — the castle household takes shape
rows.what: Every Defranceschi line in the 1709–1764 index, read letter by letter
rows.got:
**Five of the index's letters are read. Three Defranceschi children, two fathers, and a naming pattern that points at a grandfather nobody has met.**

The **G** page gives the earliest yet:

> **«Gasparo di Batta Defranceschi 10 Agosto 1718 — c. 31 t°»**

written out in full, *Defranceschi*, not the register's clipped *de Fran.chi*.

**The household so far, all from the index unless marked:**

| father | child | date | carta |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Batta** | **Gasparo** | 10 Aug 1718 | 31 t° |
| **Batta** × **Anzoletta** | **Cattarina** | 10 Feb 1728 | 66 — *entry read* |
| **Giacomo** | **Domenico Gasparo** | 9 Aug 1732 | 80 |

**Two fathers, and each names a son Gasparo.** In a parish where godparents are the judge and the vicar's wife, that is the ordinary Venetian habit of naming the first son for his grandfather — which would make **Batta and Giacomo brothers, sons of a Gasparo who is older than this volume**. *That is an inference from a naming pattern and nothing else; the 1663–1708 book, if it carries an index of its own, is where it would be tested.*

**Letters read: C, D, E, F, G.** The E page — fifty-odd Elenas and Euffemias — is clean, and so is F. **Still unread: A, B, I, L, M, N, O, P, R, S, T, V, Z**, which is where Antonio, Domenico, Zuanne, Maria, Nicolò and Pietro would sit if they are there. **Carta 31 t° and carta 80 have not been opened.**

*doc for the three index lines and for the 1728 entry on carta 66; the 1718 and 1732 entries are known from the index only.*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat index, the B page — a third child, the father's full name, and a look-alike that dissolved
rows.what: The B section of the 1709–1764 index, where Battista and Bortolo would sit
rows.got:
**One more child, the father's name in full at last — and one line that looked like the name and is not.**

**The hit.** Second from the foot of the **B** page:

> **«Battistina fig.a di Gio Batta Defranceschi 23 Xbre 1731 — c. 76 t°»**

So the father this archive has been calling **«Batta»** from the 1728 entry is **Gio Batta — Giovanni Battista**, and he has a third child: **Battistina, 23 December 1731**, named for himself.

**The household as it now stands:**

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **Gio Batta × Anzoletta** | Gasparo | 10 Aug 1718, c. 31 t° |
| | **Cattarina** | 10 Feb 1728, c. 66 — *entry read* |
| | Battistina | 23 Dec 1731, c. 76 t° |
| **Giacomo** | Domenico Gasparo | 9 Aug 1732, c. 80 |

**The miss, and it is worth writing down.** Five lines into the same page:

> «Battista fig.o di m.ro Piero **Defranzieri** 7 mag.o 1712 — c. 12»

Magnified against the Battistina line on the same page, the two endings are plainly different: **‑eschi** with its *ch* on one, **‑ieri** with a clear *r* on the other. **Defranzieri is a different surname**, and at a glance in a list it reads exactly like this one. Anyone sweeping these books should expect it. *The archive counts it as dissolved, not as a variant.*

**Letters now read: B, C, D, E, F, G.** Still to do: **A**, and **I, L, M, N, O, P, R, S, T, V, Z**.

rows.src: Anzoletta — whose wife? The 1728 entry against the archive's own 1733 line
rows.what: Whether Anzoletta is the wife of Gio Batta or of Giacomo Defranceschi, because this archive now says both
rows.got:
**Two readings, both in this archive, and they do not agree.**

The families page has long carried, from the index, *«**1733** Maria, of **Giacomo and Anzoletta**»* among the twelve fathers of the name at Svetvinčenat.

The carta 66 entry read on 20 September says *«Catta fig.a leg.ma di S.r **Batta** de Fran.chi et di **Anzoletta** sua Consorte, nata li 10 d.to»* — **1728**.

**So Anzoletta is given to two different husbands five years apart.** Three readings are possible and the archive will not pick one from a forename:

1. **Two women of the name.** Anzoletta is the Venetian diminutive of Angela and common; two households of one surname in one small town could easily hold two.
2. **A misreading on carta 66.** «Batta» and «Giacomo» do not look alike, but the entry is abbreviated and the archive has been wrong on a forename before.
3. **A remarriage.** Gio Batta's last known child is **Battistina, 23 December 1731**; Giacomo's first is **Domenico Gasparo, 9 August 1732**. That is **seven and a half months** — too short for a widow to remarry and bear a child, so if it is a remarriage the 1732 child is not hers, and the 1733 Maria might be. *Thin, but not impossible.*

**What settles it** is carta 80 for the 1732 baptism and the 1733 entry behind the families page's line: both name the mother. **Neither has been opened.** Until they are, this archive holds two Anzolettas and says so rather than quietly merging them.

*pending — and flagged because a silent merge here would invent a household.*

rows.src: The mothers of the Svetvinčenat children — got from the index, not the film
rows.what: Who the wives were behind Gio Batta and Giacomo, and whether the two Anzolettas are one woman
rows.got:
**Four index entries answer it, and they turn a name-clash into a remarriage.**

A date-filtered sweep of the persona index for **1710–1740** — no place filter, because Svetvinčenat entries carry *«Croazia, Austria»* and nothing else, the failure this archive documented in the «Pula 1667» work — returns four rows for this household:

| child | father | mother | date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Maria | **Batta Franceschi** | **Anzoletta** | 5 Jul 1715 |
| Domenico Gasparo | **Giacomo De Franceschi** | **Maria** | 2 Apr / 9 Apr 1731 |
| Maria | **Giacomo Defranceschi** | **Anzoletta** | 4 Nov 1733 |
| Casparg *(Gasparo)* | **Jacobo De Franceschi** | **Anzola** | 26 Dec 1737 |

**Gio Batta × Anzoletta is confirmed thirteen years before carta 66** — a daughter Maria in 1715. And **Giacomo had two wives**: **Maria**, who bears Domenico Gasparo in April 1731 and then vanishes from the book, and **Anzoletta / Anzola**, who bears from November 1733.

**Which makes the timing fit exactly.** Gio Batta's last child is **Battistina, 23 December 1731**, and the household stops. Giacomo's first wife bears in **April 1731** and stops. Giacomo's second marriage produces a child in **November 1733**. **Two Defranceschi households are widowed within a year of each other, and the surviving husband of one marries the surviving wife of the other.** *That is the reading; it is inference, and this is what would prove or break it — nothing.* **Svetvinčenat's marriage register is not filmed between 1623 and 1762**, so the wedding itself cannot be reached, and a dispensation for affinity, if Batta and Giacomo were brothers, would have been recorded in exactly that gap.

**A misreading of mine that this corrects.** The volume's own D-page line was read here as *«9 Ag.to **1732**»*. The index of the same baptism gives **9 April 1731**, and the roster has carried 1731 all along. **The month and the year were both misread**; the abbreviated *Ap.le* was taken for *Ag.to*. Carta 80 would settle it on the page.

*doc for the four index rows; the remarriage is inf and labelled so.*

rows.src: Joining the corpus by household — 2,251 index rows swept and cross-matched
rows.what: Whether the disconnected people in this archive can be joined to each other mechanically, rather than one register page at a time
rows.got:
**Fifty-nine candidate generational chains, and a four-generation one at Rijeka that runs straight into this archive's own Fiume household.**

**The sweep.** Every persona-index row for *Defranceschi*, *De Franceschi* and *Franceschi* in the Croatian church books, on `q.surname` and `q.fatherSurname`, paged out: **2,251 deduped rows**, of which **1,380 name both parents**. `q.motherSurname` adds nothing — the mother is indexed under her maiden name, so the surname never matches.

**The method.** Fold each name to a consonant skeleton (so *Caralipeo*, *Caralipco*, *Carlipeo* and *decaralipeo* collapse to one woman), fold place exonyms (**Vitipolis = Fiume = Rijeka**; *Almissa = Omiš*; *Fasana = Fažana*; *Pola = Pula*), then look for a **child in one entry who becomes a father in another** — same parish, twenty to forty-five years later.

**The Rijeka chain, four generations deep:**

> **Giuseppe Defranceschi × Francesca**
> → **Valentino**, b. 1772 — who fathers **twenty-one indexed children** on **Ursula / Orsola** between **1794 and 1805**
> → **Franciscus**, b. 1797 — who fathers four more between **1833 and 1836**

Each generation is attested by index entries that name the father, and the chain closes on itself: Valentino appears as a child of Giuseppe *and* as the father of twenty-one, under five spellings of his own name (*Valentino*, *Valentinus Franciscus Xaverius*, *Valentinum Josephum Gregorium*) that the skeleton-fold brings together.

**Two more that stand up:**

* **Pula** — **Vittorio → Natale Mattio** b. 1816 → **Vittorio Giovanni** 1849. The grandson carries the grandfather's name, which is the pattern this archive already reads at Svetvinčenat.
* **Ližnjan** — **Mattio → Antonio** b. 1819 → eight children 1844–1859.
* **Omiš** — **Francesco → Giovanni** b. 1854/55/57 → eight children 1879–1892.

**And the question it raises, which this archive cannot answer today.** The Fiume household at the centre of the [Valentino page](/fiume-1626/#valentino) is **Valentino the Carnian**, made a citizen in 1739, with fifteen children between 1737 and 1757. The Rijeka chain starts with a **Giuseppe × Francesca** whose son is named **Valentino** and born about 1772. **A Valentino at Fiume in 1772 named for a Valentino at Fiume a generation earlier is exactly what a grandson looks like** — but **there is no Giuseppe among the fifteen**, and this archive has just been reminded (by Jacobus Vincentius, found this morning) that the fifteen were fourteen until today. *inf, and deliberately not asserted: the Fiume baptisms of 1758–1775 would settle whether Giuseppe is a sixteenth child.*

*doc for the index rows; the chains are **inf** — name, parish and a plausible age gap, not a stated parentage.*

rows.src: The roster audited against itself — how much of the corpus is one person entered twice
rows.what: Whether the «disconnected people» are really disconnected, or duplicates of each other arriving from different sources
rows.got:
**A good deal of it is duplication, and the rest divides into two very different problems.**

Folding all 1,221 roster rows on name, birth year, canonical place and maiden name:

* **38 groups, 83 rows, of which 45 would collapse** — same person, same place, arriving from two or three different sources. The commonest pairs are **household + myheritage** (17), **myheritage + record** (15) and **burial + myheritage** (9). *Pietro De Franceschi b. 1734 of Vodnjan is in the roster **seven times**.*
* **21 cross-place candidates** — same name and year in two places. Some are certainly one person: **Anton Rudolf b. 1890 «Klenovica | Ledenice»** is the man this archive re-read this morning, and Klenovica is *in* Ledenice parish; **Antonio b. 1897 «Middle Village | Queens»** — Middle Village is in Queens; **Camillo b. 1868 «Gologorica | Pazin»**, plus a third row at Poreč. Others — **Antonius b. 1848 «Gologorica | Pula»**, **Joannes b. 1871 «Gologorica | Ližnjan»** — are either a real move or a collision, and would each take a register to settle.
* **84 roster rows have no `/who/` page**, 63 of them from the index. **Those people cannot be linked to by anything**, because there is nothing to link to. That is the cheapest unconnectedness in the archive to fix.

**One thing the audit must not do is merge on its own.** «Maria Defranceschi b. 1757» looks like seven duplicates and is not: the rows are *Browachio*, *Buman*, *Contossich*, *Covaz*, *Dobrez* — **seven different women who married into the name at Rijeka**, distinguished only by the maiden name in brackets. And «Camillo De Franceschi, in Croatian» is a deliberate namesake row, not a stray. **The list is a worksheet, not a licence.**

*The full audit — all three lists — regenerates from `scratchpad/joins.py`.*

rows.src: Fiume baptisms, 23 November 1772 — read instead of the forty-four frames
rows.what: Whether Giuseppe × Francesca, whose son heads the Rijeka chain, belong to Valentino the Carnian's household
rows.got:
**A Helena Defranceschi stands godmother to Giuseppe's first son. That is what a grandmother does.**

The plan was forty-four frames of 1746–1750 hunting a Giuseppe. **One page answered more.** The index gives Giuseppe × Francesca **four children at Fiume** — 1772, 1774, 1776, 1778 — and the eldest son's entry is where a Fiume clerk names the company. Film image ark `3:1:3QS7-899F-WCFK`:

> **«Die 23.tia 9bris 1772.** Valentinus Franciscus Xaverius, filius legitimus **DD. Josephi, et Franciscæ jugalium Defranceschi**, heri natus, baptizavit C.us Lumaga, Levantibus D.no Francisco Tomassich **et D.na Helena Defranceschi**.»

**Valentino the Carnian's wife was Helena.** She bore fifteen children between 1737 and 1757, so in November 1772 she would be in her mid-fifties — alive, and exactly the age to hold a grandson at the font. **Godparents are the one category no index carries**, which is why this needed the page and why nobody had seen it.

**Two smaller things on the same line.** The father is **«DD.»** — the doubled *Dominus* of rank; and the celebrant is **Canonicus Lumaga**, the same name as the **«D.nus Canonicus Antonius Jacobus Lunaga»** who baptised Valentino's own son Aloysius Rochus in 1754. *One canon, two generations of the same household.*

**What it does not do.** It does not prove Giuseppe is Valentino's son. There could be another Helena Defranceschi at Fiume in 1772, and this archive has been wrong today about exactly this kind of confidence. **What it does is move the question from a naming coincidence to a person in the room.** *inf — strong, specific, and on the page.*

**The forty-four frames are still worth reading**, because a Giuseppe baptised in the 1746–1750 silence would settle it outright. *doc for the entry; inf for the descent.*

rows.src: Fiume marriages 1769–1771 — hunting Giuseppe's wedding, found somebody else's
rows.what: The marriage of Giuseppe × Francesca, because a marriage entry names both fathers and would settle the descent outright
rows.got:
**Giuseppe's wedding is not in the pages read. A different Defranceschi marriage is, and it marries into the Benzoni.**

Marriages sit in the **same bound volumes as the births** at Fiume, which is the structural fact that had been misread twice (see below). The 1753–1776 run is in **9R2X-C62**, images ~286–304. Read: **286, 291, 292, 293** — March 1769 to December 1771.

**Image 293, right page, «Die 9 Xbris 1771»:**

> **«Conjunxit in Matrimonium Can.us Decanus de Benzoni **Joannem Battam Viduum Defranceschi** et Nob.m Domicellam **Catharinam de Benzoni** in primis votis, adstantibus testibus Nob. D.no Francisco a Munier et D.no Joanne Bta Carina.»**

**This is the marriage behind two index entries this archive already held** — *Mariam Dorothæam* (1773) and *Antoniam* (1776), both of **«Joannis Baptæ Defranceschi × Catharinæ»**. It gives them a wedding date, and it gives her a surname: **de Benzoni**. He marries as a **widower**; she is a *Domicella*; the officiant is the **Canon Dean de Benzoni**, presumably her kinsman.

**And the Benzoni are already in this archive, twice, around Valentino's own children.** A **«Lib. Bar. de Benzoni»** — a free baroness — stood godmother to **Aloysius Rochus in 1754**, and **«Canonicus Simon Benzoni»** baptised **Rosalia Francisca in 1755**. In 1771 a Defranceschi marries into that family. *Whether Joannes Baptista is Valentino's kin is not established — but the Benzoni thread now runs through three generations of entries.*

*doc for the marriage; the connection to Valentino's household is **inf** and rests on the Benzoni recurrence, not on a stated parentage.*

**Still to read for Giuseppe:** images **294–304** of the same volume, covering 1772–1776.

rows.src: The Fiume reel's volume structure, got right at the third attempt
rows.what: Which images on film 005497925 hold which register, after two wrong readings in one day
rows.got:
**Each waypoint is a bound volume holding births AND marriages, and the two series do not share a date range.** That is why the frame arithmetic kept failing.

| waypoint | births | marriages |
|---|---|---|
| `9R2X-ZNT…714201` | **1734–1749** | **1734–1753** |
| `9R2X-C62…714501` | **1749–1769** | **1753–1776** |
| `9R2X-82Q…714801` | 1769–1786 | 1777–1787 |

**Two corrections fall out.** First, this archive twice read **image 203 of volume one as the 1780s** and built a warning on it about an «unsafe join». It is **1753** — the marriage series, not the baptisms, and the third digit is a 5. Second, the work-list item said the 1746–1750 read was **«forty-four frames, images 127–170»**. It is not: **volume one's births stop at 1749**, so the window straddles two volumes, and images 171 onward are marriages of 1738.

**Anchors now established by reading, not interpolation.** Volume 1 births: img 126 = 29 Jul 1745, 135 = 10 Jul 1746, 153 = 7 Sep 1748, ~8.3 frames a year, ending before img 171. Volume 1 marriages: 171 = 1738, 196 = 1749–50, 203 = 1753. Volume 2 births: img 29 = 1752, 88 = 1757, ~11.8 a year. Volume 2 marriages: 286 = 1769, 292 = 1771, ~2.8 a year.

rows.src: Fiume marriages 1769 to August 1772, read out — Giuseppe did not marry here
rows.what: The marriage of Giuseppe Defranceschi × Francesca, which would name his father and settle the Rijeka descent
rows.got:
**He is not in the book, and that is itself the finding: he married somewhere else.**

**What was read.** Volume `9R2X-C62`, marriage series, **both pages of images 286, 289, 290, 291, 292, 293, 294, 295** — March–May 1769, November 1769 to February 1770, February to October 1770, November 1770 to January 1771, January to July 1771, August to December 1771, December 1771 to February 1772, and February to August 1772. *Images 287–288, roughly June to November 1769, were not reached.*

**There is no Giuseppe Defranceschi marriage in any of it.** The only marriage of the name is the one already recorded — **Joannes Baptista, widower, to Catharina de Benzoni, 9 December 1771**.

**Why the absence means something.** Giuseppe and Francesca baptise their first child at Fiume on **23 November 1772**, and three more there to 1778. A couple baptising at Fiume from late 1772 who did **not** marry at Fiume in the three years before it almost certainly **married in the bride's own parish** and came back. **So the entry that would name Giuseppe's father exists — it is just not in this town**, and finding it means finding Francesca first.

**A caution about the Benzoni thread.** On image 289 the Benzoni also witness a marriage between two families of no relation to this one — *«D.nus Canonicus Simon Benzoni»* and *«Ill.mo D.no Josepho L.B. Baro de Benzoni»* standing for a Milord de Middenberg. **They are pervasive Fiume gentry, not a family marker**, which weakens how much the 1754 and 1755 Benzoni appearances around Valentino's children can be made to carry. *Recorded because it cuts against the reading this archive found attractive an hour ago.*

*nil for Giuseppe; the negative is worth keeping because it redirects the search out of Fiume.*

rows.src: Fiume baptisms, 12 July 1774 — the godfather is Ignatio Defranceschi
rows.what: Whether Giuseppe × Francesca, who head the Rijeka chain, belong to Valentino the Carnian's household
rows.got:
**A brother stands at the font. This is as close as the registers have come to saying it.**

Giuseppe × Francesca's second child, on film image ark `3:1:3QS7-899F-WHG6`:

> **«Die 12 julij 1774. Hellenam Margaritham Mariam filiam legitimam D.D. Josephi et Franciscæ jugalium Defranceschi, heri natam, baptizavit C.us Lumaga, levantibus **D.no Ignatio Defranceschi** et D.na Theresia Tomasich.»**

**Ignatius Francus Mattheus Defranceschi is one of Valentino's fifteen.** He was baptised at this same church on **29 July 1745** — the entry found on **image 126 of this very film** earlier the same day, and one of the four children who appear in **no index anywhere**. In July 1774 he is **twenty-eight**, turning twenty-nine.

**So two of Valentino's household now stand for two of Giuseppe's children:**

| | child of Giuseppe | godparent |
|---|---|---|
| **23 Nov 1772** | Valentinus Franciscus Xaverius | **D.na Helena Defranceschi** — Valentino's wife |
| **12 Jul 1774** | Hellena Margaritha Maria | **D.no Ignatio Defranceschi** — Valentino's son |

**Why this is stronger than the 1772 entry alone.** Helena stood godmother constantly — four times in seven frames of 1745–46 — so her name at a font proves little by itself. **Ignatius is different.** The forename is rare, he is in no index, and this archive knows of no other Ignatius Defranceschi at Fiume. A man of that name and age standing for a Defranceschi child in 1774 is **Valentino's son standing for his brother's daughter**.

**What is still not proved.** No entry yet says *«Josephus filius Valentini»*. Godparents are chosen, not inherited, and this archive has spent the day learning not to let a suggestive pattern harden. **The 1746–1749 baptism gap would settle it outright**, as would a death entry giving Giuseppe's age and father.

*doc for the entry; **inf**, and now a strong one, for Giuseppe as a son of Valentino.*

rows.src: The godparents of all four of Giuseppe's children, read one by one
rows.what: Whether any Defranceschi relative stands at the font for Giuseppe × Francesca's children — the cheapest test of the descent
rows.got:
**Two of the four carry a Defranceschi godparent, and one of those two is the finding of the day. The other two do not, and that is worth saying as plainly.**

| | child | godparents |
|---|---|---|
| **23 Nov 1772** | Valentinus Franciscus Xaverius | D.no Francisco Tomassich · **D.na Helena Defranceschi** |
| **12 Jul 1774** | Hellena Margaritha Maria | **D.no Ignatio Defranceschi** · D.na Theresia Tomasich |
| **12 Mar 1776** | Valentinum Josephum Gregorium | D.no Carolo Müller · D.na Josepha Callinesi — **no Defranceschi** |
| **8 Feb 1778** | Hellenam Ludovicam | D.no **Ludovico Henrich** · D.na **Hellena Carina** — **no Defranceschi** |

**The 1774 entry is the one that matters** and has its own row. **The 1776 entry is the honest counterweight**: if the household were tightly bound to Valentino's, one might expect the name more often than twice in four. Godparents at Fiume were as much about patronage as blood — Müller and Callinesi are burgher names, and the 1772 and 1778 entries pair a Defranceschi with a Tomassich or a Henrich.

**One thread of continuity, offered at its true weight.** Three of the four were baptised by a **Lumaga** — in 1778 *«D.nus Canonicus Antonius Jacobus de Lumaga»*, which is the **same canon who baptised Valentino's own son Aloysius Rochus in 1754**, twenty-four years earlier. *He also baptised much of the town, so it is continuity of a parish, not of a family.*

**The 1778 godmother has since been resolved, and she is not one.** The line reads *«…baptizavit D.us Canon.us Antonius Jacobus de Lumaga, levantibus D.no **Ludovico Henrich** et D.na **Hellena Carina**»*. **Carina** is a Fiume name already in this archive — a *D.no Joanne Bta Carina* witnessed the Defranceschi–Benzoni marriage of December 1771. **So the score is settled at two of four**, and it settled against the archive's own hope.

*doc for all four entries; the descent stays **inf**.*

rows.src: Fiume baptisms, volume 1 images 138-140 - the sweep resumed
rows.what: A Giuseppe born to Valentino and Helena in the 1746–1749 silence — the sweep resumed at image 138
rows.got:
**Three more frames clear of a Defranceschi father - and the fourth line of the first page of 1747 names Helena again.**

Both pages of images **138, 139 and 140** read: **10 November 1746 to 17 February 1747**, continuous with the run already logged to 2 October 1746. **No Defranceschi stands as a father anywhere in it.**

But image 140, right-hand page, first entry:

> **«Die 26 Januarij 1747.** Maria Francisca filia legitima Laurentij et Catharinæ jugalium Deggini, nata 23 hujus, baptizata est… patrini fuerunt D.nus Cosar, **et Helena Defranceschi.**»

**That is the fifth time this archive has caught her**, after four appearances in images 127–133 (August 1745 – May 1746). **Valentino the Carnian's wife was Helena**, and no other Helena Defranceschi is documented living at Fiume in these years — so on residence alone the recurring godmother is his wife.

**One detail corroborates it and one warns against it.**

*For:* here in 1747 she is written **plain «Helena Defranceschi»**, no style. At Giuseppe's first child in **1772** she is **«D.na Helena Defranceschi»**. That is exactly the trajectory of the household itself — the register writes plain *Valentinus* in the 1740s and **D.nus Valentinus** from the 1750s. The same woman, before and after the family was styled.

*Against:* **five appearances in fourteen frames makes her a habitual godmother**, not a kinswoman summoned for kin. Her standing for Giuseppe's son in 1772 is therefore worth **less** as evidence of descent than it first looked, and this archive has already walked that claim back once. What the 1747 entry adds is her **identity**, not her weight.

*And a real rival exists:* this archive holds a **Helena Defranceschi b. 1725, d. 1809, of Gologorica** in the Pazin hills — the right age, the wrong town, forty kilometres away. The register entries carry **no patronymic and no husband**, so nothing inside them distinguishes the two. The identification rests on residence and on nothing else, and is filed **inf**.

rows.src: The FamilySearch index, hunting a death entry for Giuseppe Defranceschi of Fiume
rows.what: Giuseppe's own burial, which would give his age and so his birth year
rows.got:
**Nil, and the nil is worth recording because a death entry is the one document that would end this item outright.**

A Fiume burial for Giuseppe would give his **age** — and Croatian death entries of the period routinely give the father — so it would date his birth and name his parent in one line. The index was swept for every *Joseph / Giuseppe* of the surname: **36 rows**. **Exactly one is death-typed**, and it is not him:

> «Giuseppe Defranceschi — 1784;1819 — Birth, Burial, Death — Regnum Croatiæ» `3:1:3QS7-899X-KWTB`

**Born 1784.** Our Giuseppe was fathering children from 1772. A different man, probably a grandson.

So **the index holds no death for Giuseppe × Francesca's Giuseppe**, which is this film's normal state for this family rather than evidence of anything. The route stays open but has to be **browsed**: Fiume **Deaths 1702–1765** (`9R26-YWG`) and **Deaths 1766–1815** (`9R26-YWL`). He is not in the first; the second is where he would be, and it is unread.

rows.src: Fiume baptisms, film 005497925 image 146 - the 1746-1750 gap swept frame by frame
rows.what: A son of Valentino born in the 1746–1750 gap who could be Giuseppe of the Rijeka chain
rows.got:
**A sixteenth child, and the five-year silence was never silent.**

The sweep was looking for a **son** — a Giuseppe who could be the father of the Rijeka chain. On **image 146, left-hand page**, under **«Die 13 8bris 1747»**, it found a **daughter** instead:

> **«Franciscam Matthæam filiam legitimam D.ni Valentini, et Helenæ jugalium Defranceschi, natam 10 hujus, baptizavit D.nus Canonicus Hieronymus Moroldo. Patrini fuerunt Ill.mus D.nus Joannes Jacobus Irene et Nob. D.na Elisabeth Moroldi.»**

*(The godfather's surname is the one uncertain word on the page and is given as read.)*

**This is not Matheus Franciscus.** That son was baptised **17 September 1739** and has his own ark. Francisca Matthæa is a **new person**, the **sixteenth child** of the household, and she appears in **no index anywhere**.

**What it costs the archive, and what it is worth.**

*It costs a published claim.* This site said the household produced **fifteen** children and that its **1746–1750** hole was «a five-year silence in a household that otherwise produces a child every year or two». That silence was the whole reason to think an unrecorded **Giuseppe** might be hiding in it. **The silence was an artefact of the index and of an incomplete read**, and one frame of honest sweeping ended it.

*It is worth the method.* Four of this household's unindexed children were recovered in September by **interpolating between dated frames** — you need a date to aim at. **Nothing pointed at Francisca Matthæa.** She came out of reading pages that no index, no interpolation and no search could have nominated, which is the argument for sweeping a gap rather than querying it.

*And the family's own count survives.* The tradition says **ten sons**; the sixteenth child is a **daughter**, so the sons still come out at ten and the household is now **ten sons and six daughters**.

**One correction falls out of the same line.** This archive dated the family's rise in the register to «the 1750s». Here in **1747** the clerk already writes **D.ni Valentini** and stands **Ill.mus** and **Nob.** over the font. The elevation is visible three years earlier than published.

**Frames read in this sweep:** images **138–146**, both pages — *10 November 1746 to 16 October 1747*, continuous. Besides Francisca Matthæa, **no Defranceschi stands as a father** anywhere in it, and **Helena Defranceschi stands godmother four more times** (26 Jan, 26 Feb, 26 Mar and 30 Jul 1747).

rows.src: Fiume baptisms, film 005497925 image 150 - Giuseppe's own baptism, and a second Defranceschi household
rows.what: A Defranceschi son born in the 1746–1750 gap who could be the Giuseppe of the Rijeka chain
rows.got:
**Giuseppe has a birth entry, and it names a father this archive was not looking for.**

**Image 150, right-hand page** (`3:1:3QS7-L99F-W4CK`):

> **«Die 29 May 1748. Josephum Aloysium filium legitimum D.ni **Joannis Baptæ** et D.næ **Magdalenæ** jugalium **de Franceschi**, natum 24 hujus, baptizavit D.nus Canonicus Eustachius Sauf. Patrini fuere D.nus Josephus Voxila et D.na Eleonora Franul.»**

**A second Defranceschi household at Fiume.** Every Fiume entry this archive held belonged to **Valentino × Helena**. This one does not: **Joannes Baptista × Magdalena**, styled *D.nus* and *D.na*, baptising in the same church in the same decade. **Joannes Baptista is not one of Valentino's sons** — the only one of that name, *Vitus Joannes Baptista*, was baptised in **1751** and cannot father a child in 1748.

**Why this is the answer to work-list 142, and not the answer it expected.**

The item asked whether **Giuseppe × Francesca**, who head the Rijeka chain, were a missing child of Valentino the Carnian. The register says Giuseppe was a child of **Joannes Baptista**.

| what lines up | |
|---|---|
| **forename** | *Josephum Aloysium* — the *Giuseppe* of the 1772–1778 entries |
| **age** | born 24 May 1748, so **24** when his first child is baptised in November 1772 |
| **the father, independently** | this archive already found **«Joannes Baptista Defranceschi, widower»** marrying **Catharina de Benzoni on 9 December 1771** — a widower is what a man whose wife *Magdalena* has died is |
| **a date already in the tree** | the MyHeritage tree carries **Giuseppe Defranceschi b. 1748, d. 1778** at Rijeka (`mh 4510404`) with **no source at all**. The register now supplies one, and **1748 was right** |
| **and why the entries stop** | his last child is baptised **8 February 1778**, and the tree's death year is **1778** |

**What it does not settle.** No entry yet says *«Josephus filius Joannis Baptistæ»* in 1772; the identification rests on forename, surname, town, age and the father's independently attested widowerhood. It is **inf**, and it is much stronger than anything this item had.

**And it explains the first son's name without needing Giuseppe to be Valentino's child.** Giuseppe's eldest is christened **Valentinus** in 1772 — which is what you do for a grandfather *or* for the head of the family you belong to. **Helena Defranceschi at that font in 1772 and Ignatio Defranceschi at the next in 1774 are then the other household standing for its kin**, which is a better fit than either being a parent. **The open question is no longer «which of Valentino's children is Giuseppe» but «how are Joannes Baptista and Valentino related»** — and that is answerable, because **their marriages are on this same reel**: volume 1 carries **marriages 1734–1753** from about image 171, and a marriage entry names a father and usually a birthplace.

**Frames read in this stretch:** images **147–150**, both pages — *22 November 1747 to 11 June 1748*. Besides this entry, no Defranceschi stands as a father, and **Helena Defranceschi stands godmother once more** (17 December 1747), her ninth.

rows.src: Fiume marriages, film 005497925 image 168 - Valentino's own wedding
rows.what: The marriages of the two Fiume Defranceschi households, which would say how they are related
rows.got:
**«Ex Carnia» is in the register, in the clerk's own hand, and Valentino's wife finally has a maiden name.**

**Image 168, right-hand page**, second entry (`3:1:3QSQ-G99F-W428`):

> **«Die 28 Februarij 1737. D.num **Valentinum de Franceschi ex Carnia**, et **Elenam Surcho** junxit in matrimonium D.nus Petrus Eustachius Sauss Canonicus, præsentibus testibus Nob. D.no Petro Petrini et Nob. D.no Antonio Moretti.»**

*(The bride's surname is underlined in the register. The initial is the tall looped capital this hand uses for both S and Z, so **Surcho** or **Zurcho** — most likely the Italianised form of a Kvarner **Žurko / Zurco**. Given as read.)*

**Three things at once.**

**1. The date fits the household exactly.** Valentino's eldest, *Josepha Catharina*, was baptised **26 November 1737** — **nine months less two days** after the wedding. The marriage was not found by interpolation; it was found by walking the marriage run backwards from 1746 until the years ran out.

**2. «Ex Carnia» is now primary.** This archive has carried Kobler's *«Valentino Defranceschi, venuto dalla Carnia, fu fatto Cittadino nel 1739»* as a nineteenth-century historian's statement. **The parish register says it too, in 1737, two years before the citizenship** — and it says it at the moment it mattered, when a stranger married into the town. *(doc.)*

**3. His wife was not just «Helena».** Every entry for twenty years calls her *Helena* or *Elena jugalis Defranceschi*. Here, once, before she took the name, she is **Elena Surcho** — and a maiden name is a door into her own family.

**And a published claim is wrong by thirteen years, not three.** This archive said the register styled the father *D.nus* «by the 1750s»; a correction issued earlier today moved that to **1747**. **It is 1737** — he is **«D.num Valentinum»** on his wedding day, before a single child was born. He was styled from the moment he appears.

**What the entry does not give:** **no father**. Fiume marriage entries of this decade name the celebrant and the witnesses but not the couple's parents, so this does not reach back into Carnia by filiation — only by origin.

**Frames read:** images **168, 169, 170** and **189**, both pages — marriages of *November 1736 – February 1738* and *October 1746 – January 1747*. The run moves at roughly **2.2 frames to the year**.

rows.src: Fiume marriages 1736-1748, film 005497925 images 168-191, read end to end
rows.what: The marriage of Joannes Baptista × Magdalena, which would name his father and his birthplace
rows.got:
**Twenty-four frames, forty-eight pages, twelve years — and exactly one Defranceschi marriage in all of it.**

The question was **how Joannes Baptista de Franceschi relates to Valentino the Carnian**, and the plan was to put their two marriage entries side by side. **Only one of the two is there.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Found** | **Valentino × Elena Surcho, 28 February 1737** (image 168R), *«D.num Valentinum de Franceschi ex Carnia»* |
| **Found** | **Valentino as a witness**, 28 February 1740 (image 175L): *«præsentibus testibus D.no Valentino Defranceschi, et D.no Gregorio Rossani»* — three years to the day after his own wedding, and an occurrence in no index |
| **Not found** | **Joannes Baptista × Magdalena.** Nowhere between **November 1736 and February 1748** |

**The nil is the finding, and it points the same way Kobler does.**

Their son **Josephus Aloysius was born 24 May 1748**, so the marriage had to fall inside the swept window if it happened at Fiume. **It did not.** So **Joannes Baptista married outside the town** — which is precisely what a man who *arrived* does, and precisely what his son Giuseppe would do a generation later, marrying Francesca somewhere this archive still cannot name.

**And it makes Kobler's sentence testable in a new place.** Carlo De Franceschi wrote that a *«Giovanni Batt. De Franceschi venuto dalla **Contea di Pisino**… intorno al **1740***» was *«senz'altro proveniente dalla mia famiglia»* — his own, the Gologorica house. His pedigree says that man **studied at Fiume** and **married a lady of the D'Agnese family**. If our Joannes Baptista is him, **the marriage is in the County of Pazin, not at Fiume**, and **Magdalena's maiden name is the test**: *D'Agnese confirms it, anything else kills it.* That is a read of Pazin's own books, which run from 1582 and **have never been opened by this archive**.

**One near-miss, recorded so nobody chases it twice.** Image 187R, 21 December 1745, a gentry wedding in a private oratory, witnessed by *«Perill.ri D.no **Josepho Defranchi**»*. **That is de Franchi, not de Franceschi** — a different surname that reads like ours at page scale. Checked under magnification and set aside.

**Also passing through these pages:** the clerk writes origins freely — *ex Carnia*, *ex Carniolia*, *ex Insula Bergi*, *ex Parochia Vergnacco* — so **Carnia and Carniola are distinguished in the book itself** and must not be folded together. Two other Carnians marry here in these years, **Gregorio Bessora (1748)** and **Laurentius Puvet ex Luita in Carnia (1741)**, neither connected to this family.

rows.src: The County of Pazin marriage books, scoped against the parishes Kobler's family actually lived in
rows.what: Where a marriage of Joannes Baptista de Franceschi could be found, and where it could not
rows.got:
**Before reading thirty-eight frames of one parish, the shelf was counted — and it is much shorter than the question needs.**

Item 143 turns on **Magdalena's maiden name**, and Kobler puts the man who would be her husband in the **Contea di Pisino** around 1740. So: which County of Pazin parishes have **marriage books covering 1740–1748** in the FamilySearch Croatia collection this archive can reach?

**Two.**

| parish | marriages | covers the window |
|---|---|---|
| **Pazin** | 1597–1635, **1656–1852** | yes |
| **Tinjan** | **1703–1896** | yes |
| Boljun | 1640–1667 | no |
| Lupoglav (Pazin) | — | no marriages filmed |
| Stari Pazin | — | begins 1826 |
| Kringa, Sv. Petar u Šumi | — | begin 1838–1840 |

**And the parishes that matter most are not filmed here at all.** **Gologorica**, **Gračišće**, **Pićan** and **Žminj** appear in **none** of the collection's 43 Istrian parishes. Gologorica is the house with **ANNO·DOMNI·1711** cut over the door; Gračišće is where this line's earliest dated ancestor farms house 5 in 1787. **Their registers exist — this archive has quoted them through Kobler and the Blažević material — but they are not in this collection, so no amount of reading here will reach them.**

**That bounds item 143 honestly.** A negative result at Pazin and Tinjan would **not** disprove Kobler; it would only mean the marriage is in a book this archive cannot open online. *The positive case is still worth the read, and the negative case must not be over-read.*

**Tinjan is the better bet of the two, and the archive's own material says so.** Darovec, already quoted on this site, places the Friulian-Carnian stratum in *«Pazin, Pićan, Gradišće, Žminj and **Tinjan**»* — four of those five are unfilmed, and Tinjan is the one that is not.

**The Pazin volume is enumerated and anchored**, so whoever runs it does not start cold: waypoint `9R26-16F:391644801,392372801,392373301`, **396 frames**, of which **index 134 = January 1741**, **index 142 = 1746**, **index 160 = October 1747 – January 1748**. **The window is about frames 128–165.** The arks are in `scratchpad/pazin/arks.lst`.

*A caution for the reader: this volume binds three runs together — 1597–1635, 1656–1852 and 1812–1847 — so frame order is not simply chronological and the density varies. Anchor by reading, not by interpolating.*

rows.src: Tinjan marriages 1741-1749, read frame by frame for a de Franceschi groom
rows.what: A marriage of Joannes Baptista de Franceschi to a Magdalena, in the county Kobler names
rows.got:
**Nine years of a County of Pazin parish, and the surname is not in it — nor is any surname like it.**

Tinjan was read first because the archive's own material pointed here: **Darovec** places the Friulian-Carnian stratum in *«Pazin, Pićan, Gradišće, Žminj and **Tinjan**»*, and Tinjan is the only one of those five whose registers are in this collection.

**Marriages (Vjenčani) 1703–1896**, waypoint `9R2D-928:391644801,392408601,392409001`, **167 frames**. Anchored by probing: **frame 4 = 1703–1709**, **frame 9 = 1733–1735**, **frame 13 = 1749**, **frame 17 = 1757–1760**, **frame 34 = 1780**. *The volume is not linear — the first fifty years occupy nine frames and the 1780s occupy one apiece — so every date here was read, not interpolated.*

**Frames 9–13 read, both pages: 1733–1735 and 1741–1749.** **No Defranceschi, De Franceschi or Franceschi appears as groom, bride, father or witness.**

**What is there instead is the answer to a different question.** The grooms are **Červar, Milinarić, Brajećvić, Antolović, Dobrić, Šubić, Brencšev, Smokovac, Milohanić, Jurčović, Dobrila, Vitović, Grabsić, Žadanović** — **a Croatian village parish, marrying its own**, for a solid decade. The only Italian names in these pages belong to the **clerical and notarial class who witness everything**: *Antonio Floriani*, *Francisco Lasari*, *Georgius Ant. Florianis*, *Nicolaus Bottegaro*. **That is a useful negative in itself:** it says an incoming Carnian family is **not** quietly marrying into Tinjan in these years, which is what the Darovec quotation might have led this archive to assume.

**One honest gap. 1736–1740 was not found.** Frame 9 ends in 1735 and frame 10 opens *«Conjuncti sub Par.o Joanne… 1741»* — a new priest's section. Either the register has a gap there or those years sit elsewhere in a volume that is already known to run out of order. **Since Josephus Aloysius was born 24 May 1748, a marriage as late as 1747 is covered and a marriage in 1736–1740 is not** — so this read narrows the question rather than closing it.

**And it cannot close it in any case.** *A nil at Tinjan is not evidence against Kobler*, because **Gologorica, Gračišće, Pićan and Žminj — the parishes his family actually lived in — are not in this collection at all.**

*Arks saved to `scratchpad/pazin/tinjan.lst`. Pazin's own marriage volume, 396 frames with the window at 128–165, remains unread.*

rows.src: Pazin marriages, the volume re-anchored after a misread digit sent it thirty years wrong
rows.what: Where 1740–1748 actually sits in the Pazin marriage volume
rows.got:
**The frame window this archive published a few hours ago was wrong by about thirty years, and the cause was one digit.**

The Pazin marriage volume was anchored by probing and reading date headings — which is the rule — and the readings were **1741** at frame 134, **1746** at 142, **1747** at 160. From those the window for 1740–1748 was published as **frames 128–165**.

**They are 1711, 1716 and 1717.** In this clerk's hand the **4** is written with a nearly closed bowl and an almost horizontal crossbar, and at page scale it is not distinguishable from his **1** with its heavy entry stroke. The mistake is invisible from a single frame, because *«Die 27 Januarij 1711»* and *«… 1741»* are equally plausible sentences.

**What broke it open** was frame **143**, whose right-hand page carries **«1717» twice in a clean hand**. With 143 fixed at 1717, a frame 8 earlier could not be 1746.

**The volume, re-anchored — every one of these read, and the ambiguous ones cross-checked against a neighbour:**

| frame | year |
|---|---|
| 134 | 1711 |
| 142 | 1716 |
| **143** | **1717** — the anchor that broke the error |
| 178 | **1733** |
| 198 | **1742** |
| 200 | blank leaf |
| **205** | **a microfilm resolution target** — a volume boundary |

**About 2.2 frames to the year** from 178 to 198, steady.

**So the window for 1740–1748 is frames ≈194–204**, not 128–165 — and it runs into the boundary at 205, so the last years of the window may continue in the section after the target. **Eleven frames and a join, rather than thirty-eight in the wrong place.**

**The method lesson is narrower than «anchor by reading», which this archive already says.** *Reading is not enough when the digit itself is ambiguous.* A year is only anchored when it is either **written unambiguously** or **cross-checked against a neighbouring frame** — and a run's plausibility is a test: 143 being 1717 while 142 was read 1746 should have been caught the moment both were written down.

*Nothing was read on the strength of the wrong window; the error was found while setting up to read it.*

rows.src: Pazin marriages 1740-1748, read end to end across the item break
rows.what: A marriage of Joannes Baptista de Franceschi to a Magdalena, in the seat of the county Kobler names
rows.got:
**Nine years of the County of Pazin's own seat, and the surname is not in them either.**

**Marriages (Vjenčani)**, waypoint `9R26-16F:391644801,392372801,392373301`, **396 frames**. Read: **frames 194–199** and **208–216**, both pages each.

| frames | years |
|---|---|
| 194–199 | **Dec 1740 – Nov 1742** |
| 200–202 | blank leaves, then **«END OF ITEM»** title card at 203 and a resolution target at 205 |
| 208–216 | **1743 – Nov 1748** |

**No Defranceschi, De Franceschi or Franceschi — as groom, bride, father or witness — anywhere in it.**

**The structure is the thing worth recording.** The catalogue calls this one volume, *«Marriages 1597–1635, 1656–1852, 1812–1847»*, and it is **three filmed items spliced onto one reel**. The 1656– run **stops dead at November 1742** on carta 150, is followed by blank leaves, an **END OF ITEM** card and a microfilm resolution target, and then **resumes at 1743** in the next item. *Anyone interpolating a frame number across that join lands in the wrong decade* — which is exactly what happened here earlier today, by a different route.

**The names are the same answer Tinjan gave.** Sgrablich, Mattesich, Mattich, Cerovaz, Brattulich, Sironich, Mogorovich, Jaklinich, Zambarel, Cosicich, Bradicich — **an Istrian town marrying its own**, with the few Italian and German names (Franul de Waisenthuren the Praepositus, Bartholomaeus Mattich the chaplain) belonging to the men who **officiate and witness**, not to the couples.

**So both filmed parishes of the Contea di Pisino are now read for the window, and both are nil.** Tinjan 1741–1749, Pazin 1740–1748. **Joannes Baptista de Franceschi did not marry in either.**

**That does not touch Kobler.** **Gologorica, Gračišće, Pićan and Žminj — the parishes his family lived in — are in no part of this collection.** The online shelf for this question is now **exhausted**, and what remains is an **errand**: the Državni arhiv u Pazinu holds the books themselves.

*Arks: `scratchpad/pazin/arks.lst` (0–179) and `arks175.lst` (175–234).*

rows.src: FamilySearch's index of the Udine registers Antenati will not serve
rows.what: Whether FamilySearch's index reaches the Udine registers Antenati has been refusing
rows.got:
**Eight rows of this work list have been stalled on Antenati returning 403. The same registers are indexed on FamilySearch, and searching the index reaches the entries without ever asking Antenati for an image.**

**The collection is *Italia, Udine, Stato Civile (Archivio di Stato), 1806-1815, 1871-1911*** — the very series David's tree cites twenty-six times. The persona index takes **`q.anyPlace`** (`f.recordPlace` returns nothing, and `f.collectionId` does not bind), so it is searched **comune by comune**.

**Nine records of the name in Carnia, and eight of them at Paluzza and its hamlet Naunina** — **none of the nine was in this archive**:

| person | date | place | parents | id |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Daniele** | **1782** | Paluzza | **Zuanne De Franceschi & Maria Delli Zolti** | `QP7R-2RH5` |
| Francesco | 14 Dec 1807 | **Naunina**, Paluzza | Francesco & Domenica Englaro | `QPWY-QJ31` |
| Pietro Antonio | 5 Jun 1810 | Paluzza | Francesco & Domenica Englaro | `QPWT-D4GH` |
| Maria Anna | 9 Nov 1810 | Paluzza | **Daniele & Maria Silverio** | `QPHF-BBQ8` |
| Cattarina | 22 Dec 1811 | Paluzza | Francesco & **Cattarina Delli Zotti** | `QPW5-HCB4` |
| Pietro | 1851 | Paluzza | Daniele & Maria Pittino | `QGRV-ZPW8` |
| Maria | 1865 | Paluzza | Costantino & Giovanna Lazzara | `QGRJ-G6H6` |
| Egidio **Soravito** De Franceschi | — | Ovaro | Sebastiano Soravito De Franceschi & Giacoma Gortani | `QGRV-97Y7` |

**This opens the second door.** This archive has said for weeks that **Paluzza — one valley east of Mione, in the same Carnia — is the nearest thing it has to a second door into the Val di Gorto**, and that it was unworked. **It is now four generations deep**: *Zuanne* → *Daniele* (1782) → *Maria Anna* (1810), with a second *Daniele* fathering at Paluzza in 1851 and a *Costantino* in 1865.

**Two things the index hands over for free.** The mothers' surnames give the household its neighbours: **a Delli Zolti marries Zuanne and a Delli Zotti marries Francesco a generation later** — the same family, spelt two ways, married into this one twice. And **there are two Francescos or one who remarried**: *Domenica Englaro* on the 1807 and 1810 children, *Cattarina Delli Zotti* on the 1811. Unresolved, and recorded as unresolved.

**One scope question, raised deliberately.** *«Soravito De Franceschi»* at Ovaro is a **compound Carnian surname**. Whether it belongs inside a one-name study of *De Franceschi* is a decision this archive has never made. It is on the roster now so that the decision gets made rather than avoided.

*Mione and Ovaro themselves returned nothing of the name in the window — their apparent hits are Pordenone, Venezia and Valdagno, matched on the bare surname. And the Francescone/Francesconi of Udine city are a different surname and are not taken.*

rows.src: The Hreljac index, searched for Ruža's father at Fužine
rows.what: Lovre Hreljac and Dragica Vlahović of Fužine, Ruža's parents
rows.got:
**Hreljac is a Vinodol surname, and it is not a Fužine one — which redirects this item.**

The FamilySearch index was searched for **Hreljac at Fužine**, for **Lovre Hreljac** anywhere in Croatia, and for a marriage to a **Vlahović**. **No Hreljac record at Fužine at all.** What the surname does have is a tight cluster twenty kilometres away: **Grižane, Tribalj, Bakar** — the Vinodol, *the same valley as Crikvenica, Ledenice and Klenovica*, where this archive already works.

**One candidate, and it is a good one.** **«Lovra Hreljac, born and baptised 4 September 1883 at Grižane, Modruš-Fiume»**, son of **Stepan Hreljac** and **Agna Barac** — `6YBK-YPMM`, *Croatia, Church Books, 1516–1994*. Ruža was born in **1922**, so a father born in 1883 is exactly right, and the forename is the one the family uses.

*It is `inf` and must stay `inf`:* nothing ties this Lovra to Fužine or to a Dragica Vlahović. **No marriage of Lovre Hreljac to a Vlahović is indexed anywhere.**

**The redirect is the finding.** This item said to look in **Fužine marriages 1778–1857 and births 1725–1889**. If the Hreljac came from the Vinodol, **Fužine is the wrong parish for the household and only the right one for the wedding** — and **Grižane's books are the ones to read**. That also puts Ruža's father's family in the same valley as her husband's, which nobody here had noticed.

rows.src: Gologorica's Glagolitic record, dated — and what it does not say about this family
rows.what: A Glagolitic inscription at Gologorica tied to the name
rows.got:
**The village was writing Glagolitic a hundred and fifty years before the De Franceschi house was built, and the family is not in any of it.**

Gologorica's Glagolitic inscriptions, from the Istrian encyclopaedia's own entry:

| what | when | where |
|---|---|---|
| Glagolitic inscription on the **discarded base of a stone holy-water vessel** | **1549** | the chapel of All Saints, on the cemetery south of the village |
| **Glagolitic graffiti** | **15th–16th century** | the north wall of the church of the Blessed Virgin Mary *«kod lokve»*, by the pond |
| Inscription of the priest **Juraj Kaligarić** | **1595** | the north chapel of the parish church of SS Peter and Paul |

**And the house, in the same entry:** *«jednokatna je kuća obitelji **De Franceschi**, građena **1711.**, s velikim grbom i natpisom te reljefom Isusa Krista»* — a single-storey house with a **large coat of arms and an inscription and a relief of Christ**, called *«skromna palača seoskih posjednika, funkcionalna i jednostavna»* — **a modest palace of village landowners**.

**One honest deflation, and it is the point of this row.** The fragment that opened this item — *«Natpis je vjerojatno registriran u Gologorici, gdje su Defranceschi…»* — reads as though the family were **named in** a Glagolitic inscription. **Nothing found says that.** The likelier completion is *«…where the Defranceschi had their house»* — the family as the **location**, not the content. *Until Fučić's entry itself is read, this archive should not claim a Glagolitic inscription naming the name.*

**What it does give is better than a coincidence of names.** It dates the village's literacy: **Gologorica was a Glagolitic, Croatian-writing parish from at least 1549**, and the De Franceschi arrived into it and in **1711** cut **arms and a Latin-letter inscription** over their door. *That is the family's social position in one sentence, and it is on the house.*

*Fučić's **Glagoljski natpisi** (JAZU 1982, Djela knj. 57) remains unread here — it is the corpus, and its Gologorica entry is what would settle the wording.*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat births index — L read clean, M gives three children
rows.what: Defranceschi children at Svetvinčenat after 1707, in the volume's own index
rows.got:
**The M page gives two Defranceschi children, and both are after 1707, which is where this archive's reading of the parish stopped.**

| entry | carta |
|---|---|
| **«Maria d' m.ro Nardo defranceschi, 13 Agosto 1709»** | **13 tergo** |
| **«Marina di Piero Defranceschi, 21 Febraro 1710»** | **6** |
| **«Maria di Batto Defranceschi, 13 Luglio 1716»** | **26** |

**Maria continues a household this archive already holds.** The 1707 register has a boy **Piero baptised twice**, 6 and 15 October, to a father written **Nardo** once and **Lunardo** once and a mother **Eufemia** both times. *Maria of 1709 is that house, two years on.*

**Marina opens a second one.** Her father **Piero** cannot be the infant of 1707, so he is an older man — and the name is already in this parish as a patronymic: *«M.ro Ant.o di Franceschi **di Piero**»*, 25 October 1667. **Same man, or grandfather and grandson? Open.**

**And Maria of 1716 is the earliest child of Batta's house.** *Batta* was known here for **Gasparo (1718)**, **Cattarina (1728)** and **Battistina (1731)**; this comes **two years before Gasparo**. *Carta 26 would give the mother — which bears directly on the conflict this item already carries, where carta 66 gives Batta's wife as **Anzoletta** in 1728 and the families page gives a 1733 Maria to **Giacomo** and Anzoletta.*

**The L page is clean.** *Lucia* and *Lorenzo*, about ninety lines covering **1711–1733** — Bortanovich, Puttianaz, Bursich, Stancovich, Percovich, Stoicovich, Zuranich, Biljanaz, Scoblich, Millovan, Suelich, Brattlich, Bergamo, Cherbavaz, Bellijanaz, Ofrovaz, Pulcich, Vellovich, Mazzan, Ban, Salambat, Zambratio, Rusaz, Vucich, Smogliam — **and not one De Franceschi.** A clean letter is worth recording so nobody reads it twice.

**Method note for whoever continues.** The index leaf is the **right-hand page**; the left is usually blank or the tail of the previous letter. At a crop of **x 0.452–0.67, y 0.10–0.79** of the frame, in two halves, the lines are legible and a long Italian surname stands out among short Croatian ones. **The carta number sits far right, at x ≈ 0.63–0.72, and needs its own crop.**

**Letters now read: B, C, D, E, F, G, L, and M through 1717 — images 203, 204 and 205. Left: A, I, the rest of M, N, O, P, R, S, T, V, Z** — images **196 and 206–213**.
